Title: Negri Sembilan police say they are not taking sides
Article:
SEREMBAN: Police in Negri Sembilan are closely monitoring developments concerning the state's royal institution and taking necessary measures to maintain public order, without taking sides.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said police took note of the Attorney-General's Chambers' statement on the April 19, 2026 proclamation and developments in the related legal process.
In a statement, he said police respected the constitutional, legal and institutional processes.
Alzafny said police were deployed at several locations, including the Tuanku Ja'afar Royal Gallery, Balai Undang Luak Sungei Ujong and Wisma Negeri, to maintain public safety.
Police controlled access to the Wisma Negeri office for members of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council following the palace's announcement cancelling the appointments.
Alzafny said the move was to ensure security at the premises.
He said the measures should not be interpreted as police taking sides in the ongoing constitutional and legal process.
Alzafny said police would continue to carry out their duties professionally, fairly and in accordance with the law without favouring any party.
"Police will not tolerate any act that violates the law, causes provocation, disrupts public order or threatens the safety of any individual or institution."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rais Yatim arrives at Ayer Keroh court to face sedition charge
Article:
MELAKA: Former Dewan Negara president Tan Sri Rais Yatim arrived at the Ayer Keroh Court Complex at 8.30am today to face a sedition charge linked to the Negri Sembilan royal crisis.
He arrived in his own vehicle, accompanied by his wife Puan Seri Masnah Muhamat, his son and Klawang assemblyman Danni Rais, as well as his legal team.
Rais subsequently entered Sessions Court 2.
He is expected to be charged under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act 1948, punishable under subsection 4(1) of the same Act by a fine of up to RM5,000, imprisonment for up to three years, or both.
Media reports yesterday, citing the e-Court system, said the 84-year-old was scheduled to be charged before Sessions Court 2 judge Raja Noor Adilla Raja Mahyaldin.
The former Jelebu member of parliament was among those present at a ceremony in a hotel in Alor Gajah on June 5 at which Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar was proclaimed as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.
The Negri Sembilan palace later declared the proclamation invalid under the state constitution, law and customs.
Rais is also a former Umno leader and current chairman of Parti Wawasan Negara.

Title: Najib makes first public appearance since conditional pardon [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak appeared in public today for the first time since he was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest.
The former prime minister, who remains incarcerated at Kajang Prison, was brought to the High Court this morning before judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin.
Dressed in a light grey suit and white shirt, Najib arrived at 8.30am under tight security, accompanied by Prisons Department officers, some wearing black tactical gear.
His appearance was the first public sighting of the 73-year-old since the Federal Territories Pardons Board's decision was announced on Sept 18.
The decision allows Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to stipulated conditions.
For now, however, Najib remains an inmate at Kajang Prison.
His transfer to house arrest has yet to take place as the conditions attached to the pardon, including payment of a RM50 million fine, have yet to be fulfilled.

Title: Nurul Izzah pays tribute to late uncle 'Uncle Ros'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nurul Izzah Anwar has paid tribute to her late uncle, Idrus Ibrahim, fondly known as "Uncle Ros", describing him as a big-hearted man who embraced everyone with warmth and affection.
In a Facebook post, the eldest daughter of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Uncle Ros was a teacher and a cherished figure in her family.
"Uncle was a person of great spirit and boundless love, who always treated everyone with warmth and a sense of kinship," she said.
Nurul Izzah said Cheruk To' Kun and Jalan Kilang Ubi would no longer feel the same following his passing.
She said the kindness, sacrifices, contributions and love he had shown towards her father, their family and "the struggle" would, God willing, continue as accepted deeds before Allah.
She also extended her prayers to Uncle Ros' widow, Aunty Dah, his children and the rest of the family, praying that Allah would grant them strength, patience and resilience in facing the loss.
"With His grace, we shall all meet again in Jannatul Firdaus in the future. Insya-Allah.
"Al-Fatihah," she wrote.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze improves, 4 Sarawak areas record unhealthy API
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions are improving, with only four areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today.
The Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System showed Serian recording an unhealthy API reading of 180, while Samarahan and Kuching each recorded 168 and Sri Aman recorded 165.
Of the 68 API monitoring stations nationwide, four recorded unhealthy readings (101-200), while 61 recorded moderate readings (51-100) and three recorded good readings (0-50).
No stations recorded very unhealthy or hazardous readings.
The improvement was driven by rain in several states.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecast heavy rain in several areas around the Klang Valley in the afternoon.
In Sarawak, rain is also forecast in Kuching, Miri and Serian, in the morning and afternoon.
Residents in affected areas are advised to limit outdoor activities, wear face masks when outdoors and drink enough water to reduce the health effects of poor air quality.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Turkiye rejects Netanyahu's 'baseless accusations' at UN
Article:
ISTANBUL: Turkiye rejected Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's "baseless accusations" at the United Nations, its state-run news agency Anadolu reported on Friday.
Netanyahu had called Turkiye's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan a "tyrant" during a fiery speech at the UN, accusing Ankara of harbouring Hamas leaders.
The Israeli leader's address to the UN General Assembly on Thursday, in which he denounced enemies and allies alike, sparked uproar in the chamber.
Dozens of envoys from across the world walked out, some jeering and booing, while Netanyahu's own team stood and applauded, and the speaker of the session shouted for order.
"The latest country to become a super spreader of antisemitic lies (is Turkiye)," he said.
"Erdogan is a tyrant. He also hosts the Hamas terror chiefs."
[[nid:1540638]]
Erdogan has urged world leaders to "exert greater pressure on Israel" over its war in Gaza and called on nations to recognise Palestine as an independent state.
Anadolu quoted the Turkish presidency's communications director Burhanettin Duran as slamming Netanyahu's allegation as "incompatible" with UN values.
"Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's use of the UN General Assembly podium to level 'baseless accusations' against Turkiye and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan was incompatible with the 'ideals of peace, law and dialogue' represented by the UN," Duran said.
Netanyahu's words cannot "make his massacres, the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza and the proceedings before international law invisible," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit opens higher against greenback, major currencies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the greenback and major currencies on Friday, amid mixed movements in the foreign exchange market.
At 8am, the ringgit increased to 4.0810/0865 against the US dollar from Thursday's close of 4.0840/0880.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said movements in the United States (US) Treasury yields continued to influence market sentiment, with the yield on 30-year US Treasury bonds rising eight basis points to 5.48 per cent, its highest level in two decades.

Title: Nepal floods were 'a warning to the world,' prime minister tells UN
Article:
UNITED NATIONS: The catastrophic Nepal flooding last month was "not just a local tragedy, it was a warning to the world," the country's Prime Minister Balendra Shah told the United Nations on Thursday.
Shah said a warming climate was "destabilising the fragile Himalayan ecology," melting permafrost and glaciers and accelerating hazards.
He urged the international community to help bear the cost of adapting to climate change, because "Nepal cannot build resilience alone against a crisis made worse by the failure of global governance."

Title: Najib's family yet to receive house arrest SOP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Najib Razak's family has yet to receive any information, including standard operating procedures (SOPs), from authorities on his proposed house arrest.
Najib's fourth child, Nooryana Najwa, said the family and lawyers had also yet to receive any information from the Prisons Department, including details on modifications to the house to facilitate the house arrest.
"Other than that, we have yet to receive any SOPs from the Prisons Department. Simply put, we have not received any official information. Our lawyers have also not received any official information. So, we are still waiting for information from the Prisons Department.
"We really do not know. As family members, we have yet to receive any news or information from prison officers," she told Utusan Malaysia when met.
Previously, media reports said Najib was expected to serve the remainder of his prison sentence at his residence in Langgak Duta here, alone and under the supervision of the Prisons Department, with family visits also restricted.
Lawyer Datuk Hasnal Rezua Merican said the location was chosen because no family members lived there, allowing the property to be used as a prison facility, subject to criteria set by the Prisons Department director-general.
Meanwhile, Nooryana said the Langgak Duta residence had been vacant since her father was imprisoned on Aug 23, 2022.
"Mum (Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor) lives with me. So, the house has been vacant since (Najib) was imprisoned," she said.
Najib is currently serving his sentence at Kajang Prison after a conditional pardon granted by Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, on Sept 18 enabled him to serve the remainder of his sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine.
However, on the eighth day today, there was still no new development from Kajang Prison.
On the solidarity fund launched by Umno, Nooryana said she had been informed that total contributions had reached more than RM2 million.
"I understand that Umno members are not concentrated in urban areas, so it is rather difficult for us to reach the fundraising target within a short period.
"So, what Umno is doing now is bringing the fund to every programme held in rural areas to raise sufficient contributions," she said.
Nooryana said the family welcomed the decision on conditional house arrest after waiting for a long time for an update on Najib's situation.
"At the time the decision was made, Mum was with me. We were happy because at least there was a decision. There was a way out for my father.
"Although the opportunity is rather complicated for the family, we know what needs to be done," she said.
However, she said the family is still waiting for several matters to be finalised before commenting further on the implementation of the house arrest.
"Because right now, we are still waiting. There has been no final decision. So, I cannot comment beyond that.
"I know there is a lot of speculation out there. If we are to make decisions, we should base them on accurate information from the authorities," she said.
Nooryana also said the family was touched by the support shown by Umno and members of the public who had come forward with contributions to support efforts to secure Najib's release through house arrest.
"We were deeply touched when Umno announced that it would launch a solidarity fund for Datuk Seri Najib. Likewise, we are grateful for the efforts of ordinary Malaysians who have been willing to contribute.
"We are relieved that there is finally a way out. It gives hope to the family, although we understand that its implementation remains subject to the conditions set," she said.

Title: The Chias keep Teochew tradition alive, one pastry at a time [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Chia Chin Chong fights back tears as he recalls the sacrifices his father made to keep their family bakery alive.
The 26-year-old had watched his father, Chia Seng Chee, labour at Ming Yi Bakery, turning out traditional Teochew pastries to support their family of four.
"I saw how my father grew older alongside our business. He would start making pastries at 4am," he recalled.
Ming Yi began in Pulau Ketam in 1977, when Seng Chee's father, Chia Kek Leng, started making pastries while working in the family's existing catering business.
Kek Leng had learned the craft of pastry-making from a master baker and, in time, passed that knowledge and the skills that came with it to Seng Chee.
Seng Chee was exposed to the trade from the age of eight. By 15, he had left school to work in it full-time.
[[nid:1540599]]
"Coming from a small town with no other skills besides making pastries, I naturally continued learning the craft," said Seng Chee, now 56.
Today, Ming Yi Bakery, which operates from a shoplot in Klang, specialises in traditional Teochew pastries, known for their flaky textures and savoury or sweet fillings, including Hua Tao and La Gao mooncakes.
Unlike the intricately moulded Cantonese mooncakes commonly associated with the Mid-Autumn Festival, Hua Tao and La Gao are markedly different in appearance and preparation.
[[nid:1540598]]
Hua Tao are typically flat, pan-fried cakes stamped with a bakery's seal, while La Gao are steamed, chewy pastries filled with white lotus or red bean paste and often garnished with sesame seeds.
While traditional baking equipment has made way for modern appliances, Seng Chee still maintains his father's philosophy of never cutting corners and using the best ingredients.
PASTRIES AS A BRIDGE
Growing up, Chin Chong remembers the rhythms of the family business vividly.
"Every night after finishing work, my father would come home and write down a list of customers' names, and call them one by one, asking them if they would like to buy some pastries," he said.
His father would begin baking at 4am before pausing to send Chin Chong and his older sister to school before continuing to make and deliver the pastries.
[[nid:1540597]]
"Growing up, we were always helping out by his side while he worked. So, in a way, he was working and spending time with us simultaneously.
"In fact, these pastries served as a bridge of communication between my father and us," he said.
Chin Chong, who holds a degree in International Business, initially had no plans to take over the family business but had a change of heart as he did not want the family legacy to die out.
WHEN OLD MEETS NEW
But the handover from one generation to the next has not always been seamless.
Father and son sometimes clash over how the business should evolve. Chin Chong pushes for changes to packaging, marketing and recipes, while Seng Chee remains cautious about altering traditions that have sustained the bakery for decades.
[[nid:1540596]]
"Sometimes we do reach a consensus. But honestly, most of the time we don't," Chin Chong said with a chuckle.
Beneath those disagreements, however, lies one principle on which both generations remain firm: quality comes first.
For Chin Chong, preserving the family's heritage does not mean resisting change.
He hopes to introduce traditional Teochew pastries to a wider Malaysian audience while finding ways for the business to grow.
More than that, he hopes to ease the physical burden his parents have carried for years.
"Everything we have today was shaped piece by piece, pastry by pastry. All these achievements came from making one pastry at a time.
"What I hope most is that when people taste our pastries, they can realise the importance of preserving this culture and heritage," he said.
[[nid:1540595]]
For Seng Chee, the future now rests with the son who once watched him work through the night.
"I leave the future to my son. I believe he can carry on and expand our business, and it has made me very happy seeing him willing to learn this craft," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Being project-focused at work: Collaboration and purpose
Article:
IN any workplace, it is easy to become consumed by tasks. Emails arrive, meetings fill the diary, deadlines approach and problems demand immediate attention.
Yet being busy is not the same as being productive. A project-focused approach requires us to look beyond individual tasks and understand the larger purpose behind the work.
Being project-focused means having a clear understanding of what needs to be achieved, why it matters and how success will be measured. It means keeping the desired outcome in sight rather than becoming distracted by every issue that appears along the way.
This does not mean ignoring the day-to-day responsibilities of a job. Rather, it means understanding how those responsibilities contribute to a bigger objective.
When people can see the connection between their work and the final outcome, they are more likely to make thoughtful decisions about where to spend their time and energy.
Purpose is therefore an important part of being project-focused. A project without a clear purpose can quickly become a collection of activities with no obvious destination.
People may complete their individual responsibilities successfully, yet the overall result may fall short.
A clear purpose provides direction. It helps teams distinguish between what is important and what is merely urgent. It also gives people a reason to remain committed when a project becomes complicated or progress is slower than expected.
However, purpose alone is not enough. Successful projects depend on collaboration.
Most meaningful workplace projects involve people with different responsibilities, experiences, personalities and perspectives.
Expecting one person to have all the answers is unrealistic. Good collaboration recognises that different contributions can strengthen the final result.
Collaboration is more than simply dividing the workload. It involves communication, trust and a willingness to listen. Team members need to understand not only what they are responsible for, but also how their work connects with the responsibilities of others.
This connection is particularly important when projects become challenging.
If people work in isolation, small problems can remain unnoticed until they become significant obstacles. Open communication allows concerns to be raised earlier and solutions to be developed collectively.
Good collaboration also requires people to leave their egos at the door. A project should not become a competition over whose idea receives the most attention.
The central question should be: what will best serve the objective?
That does not mean every opinion will be accepted. Healthy collaboration allows people to disagree respectfully. Different viewpoints can expose weaknesses, challenge assumptions and produce better solutions.
The key is to disagree with ideas rather than with people. A project-focused workplace also requires accountability. Collaboration should never become an excuse for unclear ownership.
Every person involved should understand their responsibilities, deadlines and expected contribution.
Accountability works best when expectations are established early. When everyone knows who is responsible for what, there is less confusion and fewer opportunities for important tasks to fall between the cracks.
At the same time, accountability should not mean assigning blame whenever something goes wrong. Projects rarely proceed exactly according to plan. Circumstances change, mistakes happen and unexpected problems emerge.
A constructive team asks what can be learned and what needs to change. The objective is to solve the problem, protect the project and prevent the same issue from recurring.
Being project-focused also means being prepared to adapt. Having a plan is essential, but becoming so attached to the original plan that new information is ignored can be counterproductive.
Circumstances can change. Priorities can shift. New information can emerge.
A project-focused team understands the difference between remaining committed to the purpose and remaining rigid about the method.
The purpose should provide the anchor, while the approach can evolve when necessary.
Another important element is communication. People cannot collaborate effectively when information is unclear, inconsistent or unnecessarily complicated. Good project communication is timely, relevant and accessible.
It should also be two-way. Leaders and project managers need to communicate expectations, but they must also create opportunities for others to provide feedback, raise concerns and suggest improvements.
Ultimately, being project-focused is about moving from activity to achievement. It asks us to consider whether what we are doing is genuinely contributing to the outcome we are trying to achieve.
This requires discipline. It means being willing to prioritise, say no to unnecessary distractions and focus attention on work that makes a meaningful difference.
It also requires perspective. A successful project is rarely the achievement of one individual. It is usually the result of many people contributing their expertise towards a shared purpose.
When purpose provides direction, collaboration provides strength and accountability provides structure, projects have a stronger foundation for success.
The most effective workplaces therefore do not simply ask people to work harder. They encourage people to work with greater clarity, greater cooperation and a stronger understanding of why their contribution matters.
Being project-focused is ultimately about keeping the destination visible while bringing people together for the journey.
When everyone understands the purpose, takes responsibility for their role and works constructively with others, work becomes more than a series of completed tasks.
It becomes progress towards something that matters.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Green shipping hits rough seas
Article:
KLANG: The shipping industry's push towards greener fuels has hit rough waters, with scarce alternative-fuel supply, inadequate bunkering infrastructure and limited access to green financing slowing the transition.
The biggest constraint is the limited global supply of green methanol, which is emerging as a key bottleneck in the maritime sector's shift to cleaner fuels.
Malaysia Shipowners' Association chairman Mohamed Safwan Othman said that more ships are returning to liquified natural gas (LNG), which is not a fully zero-carbon fuel.
"We have data that showed in 2024, more than 60 per cent of the ships orderbook was methanol-powered. But things have shifted now and we see more ships are going back to LNG.
"We realised this is mainly because it is not easy to get methanol supply globally.
"Even the biggest port, which is our southern neighbour, is currently trying to source methanol from outside this region," he said at a panel discussion at the Green Ports 2026 International Conference held here today.
Besides constrained fuel supply, transition cost is also a major hurdle for industry players.
Safwan noted that although industry players want to comply with international regulations like the International Maritime Organisation's (IMO) Net Zero Framework, the framework's main concern remains the economic costs of the transition.
The framework is a global regulatory package aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions from international shipping to net zero by 2050.
"As shipowners, we want to go green and we have the technology to go green. But again, the bunkering facility and to get the right supply of fuel is really a challenge.
"And if you look at the IMO's framework, it clearly treats the ship owners a bit unfairly, especially when you talk about the imposed penalty of fines towards ship owners that do not have green fuel," he said.
Safwan underscored that shipping needs access to green financing but they are usually blocked by the Poseidon Principle.
It is a global framework that allows financial institutions and marine insurers to assess whether their ship-financing portfolios align with international climate goals.
"We had a lot of engagements with Bank Negara Malaysia in the past year. And I hope that we continue the discussion with the central bank in terms of access to green financing," he said.
However, Safwan said green transition does not always translate to high capital expenditure.
The association often advocates operational efficiency to its members to curb the rise in costs for green adoption.
He said many of the associations' members have installed a vessel fuel monitoring system, where in house data have shown that it lowered fuel consumption by more than 70 per cent.
State members at the IMO postponed the adoption of the framework last year mainly due to opposition mainly from the US, Saudi Arabia and other oil-producing nations on the framework's pricing that would raise costs for consumers and shipping companies.
The framework called for ship owners to increasingly adopt cleaner fuels from 2028 or face financial penalties.
At the April IMO meeting held in London, High Commission of Malaysia stated that Malaysia continues to advocate for approaches that are "practical, equitable and implementable" taking into account the diverse circumstances of all member states.
Johor Port Authority senior manager Ahmad Syahrir Ashaari said there are various types of methanol that can be used as fuel and the IMO's regulations call for total green fuel adoption starting from the source, which presents a challenge.
"As a port authority, we need to look back on this because in layman's terms, it means no fossil fuel from the source.
"We have to look at this thoroughly and strengthen our regulatory framework for this type of fuel," he said.
He added that the ideal fuel for the industry would be green methanol but its production is costly.
"And the market is uncertain. Ship owners will think that if they build their ships mainly for methanol or ammonia whether there will be adequate bunkering facilities?," he asked.
Under Johor Port Authority's watch, Port of Tanjung Pelepas has adopted the refueling of vessels with low-carbon fuels.
It commenced pilot bunkering operations in 2024 and completed the first operation for a Maersk dual-fuel methanol container vessel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US Democrats criticise lavish Trump-Xi summit as lacking substance
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Senate Democrats criticised President Donald Trump's summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, saying it prioritised pageantry over substance on issues such as artificial intelligence, trade, critical minerals and weapons for Taiwan.
Trump welcomed Xi to the White House for a state summit heavy on diplomatic honours, but with no sign that closed-door talks yielded breakthroughs on the issues dividing them.
In a statement signed by at least 19 of the 47 members of the Democratic caucus and seen by Reuters, the Democrats called on Trump to immediately deliver more than US$15 billion in security assistance — US$1.3 billion in funds and a US$14 billion arms sale package — that Congress has approved for Taiwan and to push for human rights and the release of wrongfully detained Americans.
Some of Trump's fellow Republicans also marked the summit by calling on Trump to release the funds for Taiwan.
The Democrats also criticised Trump's loosening of restrictions on high-end chip sales to China, and said that the extension of the US-China tariff truce does not sufficiently address supply chain issues such as China's hold on global rare earth refining.
"We will compete successfully with China only through sustained investment in our own strengths, close coordination with allies, and an unwavering defence of our democratic values," the statement said.
Democrats are typically critical of Trump's policies, but their response to the summit gave an indication of how party members might address Beijing if they take control of one or both houses of Congress in the Nov 3 midterm elections.
Polls show that Trump's Republicans will struggle to keep their slim majorities in Congress in the upcoming contest, as the president's approval rating drops.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Argentine poverty rate climbs, in setback for Milei
Article:
BUENOS AIRES, (Argentina): Argentina's poverty rate increased to 32.3 per cent in the first half of 2026, partly erasing gains made under President Javier Milei as incomes fail to keep step with rising prices, official statistics showed Thursday.
The rate grew 4.1 points compared to the last half of 2025, the national statistics agency Indec said.
The rate of extreme poverty also shot up from 6.3 per cent to 7.5 per cent.
Children were the worst hit, with 44.5 per cent of Argentines aged 14 years and younger classified as poor, and 10.8 per cent as extremely poor.
Indec considers adults who cannot afford a basic basket of goods and services valued at around US$340 (RM1,400) to be poor.
It considers those who cannot afford a more basic food-only basket worth around US$150 (RM613) to be extremely poor.
The figures deal a setback to Milei, a free-market radical, who nearly halved the poverty rate during the first two years of his mandate, mainly by shrinking perennially high inflation.
The poverty rate has swung wildly since he came to power on a promise to revive the moribund economy through drastic austerity measures and deregulation.
From a high of 52.9 per cent in the first half of 2024, following his more-than-50-per cent devaluation of the peso, the rate fell to 28.2 percent in the second half of last year.
This year's increase coincided with a rebound in inflation at the start of the year before a new decline to 1.7 per cent in August, the lowest level in 14 months.
Eduardo Donza, a researcher at the Social Debt Observatory of the Argentine Catholic University (UCA), blamed job insecurity for high poverty rates in South America's second-largest economy.
The manufacturing and retail sectors have hemorrhaged jobs due to falling purchasing power and Milei's decision to throw Argentina open to foreign competition, leading to a surge in imports.
Some 30,000 companies have closed since he took office, and unemployment rose to 7.9 per cent in the second quarter of this year, the highest level since 2021.
Economists say that, more than unemployment, poverty is being driven by the high rate of informal work.
"The biggest problem is job insecurity, not unemployment, because when families are deprived...they have to invent a job, which can be collecting waste, street vending, selling food at the train station," said Donza.
Milei claims that he has lifted 14 million people out of poverty — an estimate based on the fall in poverty from the peak it hit after he became president. — AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saudi reports fresh Houthi attacks as France offers military support
Article:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles on Thursday after issuing warnings for several regions including Makkah, as France vowed to send "military means" to help shield the key Saudi oil terminal of Yanbu.
The attacks were reported as fighting raged in Yemen between the Houthis and Riyadh-backed government forces, killing dozens of people on both sides, according to a tally from seven sources who spoke to AFP.
The missiles were the latest in a series of escalating Houthi attacks since July, when renewed hostilities shattered a years-long truce and embroiled Yemen in the wider Middle East war.
Since then, the Houthis have imposed a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, hitting its tankers and territory and seizing swathes of Yemen's Red Sea coast, which is vital for Saudi oil exports.
Their gains cement the hold of Iran and its allies on the two waterways that the wider Gulf, including top crude exporter Saudi Arabia, relies on to ship out its oil and other fuel products.
The Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen's government since 2015 against the Houthis said six ballistic missiles had been intercepted, thwarting attacks on Taif and Yanbu.
"Escalations and violations by the terrorist Houthi militia will be dealt with firmly," said coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki on X.
Earlier, the Saudi Civil Defence had issued a brief series of alerts including one for Makkah, home to Islam's holiest sites, with separate warnings for the Red Sea governorate of Yanbu as well as the Taif, Jeddah and Tabuk regions.
The alerts were lifted a few minutes later. In recent weeks, alerts have often preceded attacks by the Houthis.
Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian denied Thursday that Teheran was directing Houthi battle plans.
"The Houthis are responsible for their own actions. They don't take directions from us as those who are resisting in the region, based on the situations that have been imposed on them," Pezeshkian told Fox News, according to the broadcaster's translation of his remarks.
With pressure mounting on Saudi Arabia, French President Emmanuel Macron said France planned to "send military assets, meaning soldiers, radars and defence systems to protect" Yanbu.
The infrastructure in and around Yanbu forms a key node in Saudi Arabia's vast network of energy installations.
Yanbu serves as the kingdom's primary crude export terminal on the Red Sea and is connected to its oil-producing regions near the Gulf coast by the East-West pipeline, also known as Petroline.
Yanbu is also home to major oil storage and refining facilities, while its location on the Red Sea provides Saudi Arabia with an alternative route for sending crude and petroleum products towards European markets.
Strategic hilltops
Last week, Riyadh accused the group of targeting Makkah for the first time since 2017 with a drone that was downed, an accusation the Houthis denied.
A few days later, the group attacked the Saudi capital Riyadh — the first in years, marking a new escalation in the conflict.
As the Houthi attacks targeted Saudi Arabia on Thursday, battles raged on the ground in Yemen.
At least 150 Houthi fighters and government forces members have been killed in the past 24 hours, sources from both sides told AFP, including in clashes over hilltops overlooking the Bab al-Mandab strait at the mouth of the Red Sea.
At least 98 soldiers and government forces members were killed, according to an AFP tally compiled from five military sources.
Most were killed in Houthi ballistic missile and drone attacks, with dozens of Yemeni troops killed.
The Houthis later claimed launching a complex barrage involving ballistic missiles and drones to target command centres and weapons depots in southern Saudi Arabia, with the group saying Yemeni and Sudanese fighters were killed and injured in the attack along with Saudi personnel.
The group also claimed late Thursday to have launched attacks across the border that targeted Aramco infrastructure in Yanbu and an unnamed site in Riyadh.
At least 52 Houthi fighters were killed in other clashes, two sources from the group said.
Many on both sides were also killed in clashes in the Kahboub Mountains and in areas between the Lahj and Taiz regions, as the Houthis seek to dominate the highlands overlooking Bab al-Mandab to protect newly seized territory.
In July, a fragile 2022 truce between the Houthis and Yemen's government fell apart after the group allowed an Iranian plane to land in Sanaa in defiance of Riyadh's control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.

Title: Colombia's new US-backed government cuts ties with Iran
Article:
BOGOTA: Colombia said Thursday it had cut diplomatic ties with Iran, the latest Washington ally in Latin America to sever links with the US arch-foe.
Colombia's new right-wing president, Abelardo de la Espriella, has redrawn Colombia's alliances since taking over from his leftist predecessor Gustavo Petro on Aug 7 with the full-throated endorsement of US President Donald Trump.
Before his inauguration, De la Espriella also announced plans to sever ties with authoritarian leftist regimes in Cuba and Nicaragua, though he has yet to do so.
His government said Thursday the decision to cut ties with Iran, which took effect on Sept 19, was based on "hemispheric national security" considerations.
It accused the Iranian government of having ties to "narco-terrorist groups that threaten the security of the country", without giving proof of the allegations.
The government further lambasted Teheran for blocking traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and attacking other countries in the Middle East in its war with the United States and Israel.
Bogota added that it would maintain consular relations with Teheran.

Title: Explainer: The Mindanao peace process and the road to Kuala Lumpur
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Three decades after peace talks began, the Philippine government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) are still working to complete key parts of a 2014 agreement aimed at ending decades of conflict in Mindanao.
The two sides are due to meet in Kuala Lumpur today to discuss a roadmap for implementing the remaining commitments under the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB).
The meeting will focus in part on the normalisation programme for former MILF combatants, one of the key elements of the peace settlement.
The conflict between the Philippine government and Moro separatist groups killed more than 120,000 people and displaced millions.
The CAB provided for a new autonomous region in Mindanao and the decommissioning of MILF combatants and weapons. The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) was established in 2019 as part of the settlement.
Why Kuala Lumpur?
Malaysia has served as the third-party facilitator of the peace process since 2001.
Kuala Lumpur has hosted rounds of negotiations between the Philippine government and MILF, as well as meetings on implementation of the peace agreement. The last Peace Implementing Panel meeting hosted by Malaysia was in 2019.
Malaysia's role has included keeping communication open between the two sides and supporting implementation of the peace agreement.
The facilitation is also intended to support completion of the normalisation programme and provide continuity as political leadership changes in Manila and Bangsamoro.
Malaysia has said it will maintain a neutral and non-partisan role, while the Philippine government and MILF remain responsible for completing the outstanding provisions of the agreement.
Key dates
January 1997 — Initial contacts
The government of President Fidel Ramos opened contacts with the MILF, a breakaway group from the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF), which had signed a peace agreement with the government in September 1996.
July 1997 — Ceasefire
The Philippine government and MILF signed a ceasefire agreement, paving the way for formal talks aimed at ending the insurgency in the southern Philippines.
July 1998 — Estrada backs talks
President Joseph Estrada, after taking office, said his administration would pursue peace talks with the MILF.
March 2001 — Talks resume
The Philippine government and MILF resumed formal peace talks in Kuala Lumpur under Malaysian facilitation.
October 2012 — Framework Agreement
The two sides reached the Framework Agreement on the Bangsamoro, setting out the basis for a final peace deal and a new autonomous political entity.
March 2014 — Comprehensive Agreement
The Philippine government and MILF signed the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro in Manila on March 27, 2014.
The agreement set out the political and normalisation tracks of the settlement, including the creation of the Bangsamoro region and the decommissioning of MILF combatants and weapons.
2019 — BARMM established
The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao was established following the passage of the Bangsamoro Organic Law.
The peace process shifted from negotiations to implementation, including the normalisation programme and decommissioning of former MILF combatants.
August 2026 — Normalisation resumes
The Philippine government and MILF implementing panels met in Davao City and agreed to resume normalisation activities after a pause.
They also agreed to hold a special meeting in Kuala Lumpur.
Sept. 14, 2026 — First BARMM parliamentary election
The first parliamentary election in the BARMM was held, marking another step in the region's transition to its new political system.
Sept. 25, 2026 — Kuala Lumpur meeting
The Philippine government and MILF implementing panels are due to meet in Kuala Lumpur to discuss a roadmap for completing implementation of the CAB.
The meeting comes as the two sides seek to advance outstanding parts of the peace agreement, including the normalisation process.

Title: UN General Assembly walkout: Malaysia, Indonesia among nations protesting Netanyahu's address
Article:
UNITED NATIONS: Dozens of envoys from across the world walked out of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's speech to the UN on Thursday in protest at the Israeli leader.
Delegates jeered and booed, while Netanyahu's own team stood and applauded, and the speaker of the session shouted for order.
"If there are any other moral cowards who haven't left this hall, please do so now," Netanyahu said.
The hall, sparsely filled earlier in the session, gradually filled up before Netanyahu's speech.
The Palestinian delegation had called in a memo seen by AFP for other missions to join their own act of protest.

Title: KL hosts fresh Philippines-MILF peace talks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Philippine government and Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) negotiators are due to meet in Kuala Lumpur today to advance a peace process that began three decades ago.
The one-day Special Meeting of the Government of the Philippines (GPH) and MILF Peace Implementation Panels will focus on outstanding commitments under the 2014 Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB).
The Philippine government panel will be led by Secretary Mel Senen Sarmiento, while the MILF panel will be chaired by Mohagher Iqbal.
Malaysia's facilitator is General (Rtd) Tan Sri Zulkifli Zainal Abidin, who has held the position since 2023.
The last meeting of the two implementing panels was held in Davao City in August.
The peace talks began in 1997, while the CAB, signed in 2014, provides the framework for the peace process and contains commitments that the parties are still working to implement.
The conflict in the southern Philippines has killed more than 120,000 people and displaced about two million since the late 1960s.
Among the issues under discussion is the normalisation process, including the decommissioning of MILF combatants and weapons, transformation of former MILF camps, disbandment of private armed groups, and transitional justice and reconciliation.
As part of the peace process, the two sides are also working towards an Exit Agreement, which is intended to formally end the GPH-MILF peace process once all commitments under the 2014 Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB) have been fulfilled.
The recent Bangsamoro Parliamentary Election held on Sept 14, 2026 was an important achievement in the political track, while continued attention is given to the implementation of all commitments under the CAB.
The Kuala Lumpur meeting would focus on the remaining CAB provisions, including efforts to develop a roadmap for outstanding commitments.
The meeting will give the two sides an opportunity to discuss the next steps in implementing the agreement, with Malaysia continuing its role as facilitator.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Airbus identifies A321neo defect, says no safety risk
Article:
MEXICO CITY: Airbus said on Thursday it had identified and contained a "quality issue" in the fuselage structure of its A321neo aircraft, but that planes could continue operating as it does not pose a safety risk.
A source familiar with the matter said the defect affects about 500 aircraft, including roughly 250 already in service and 250 in production.
The A321neo, Airbus's largest and most popular single-aisle jet, seats up to 244 passengers and is designed to fly routes of up to 4,000 nautical miles.
It is the second industrial problem to affect the fuselage of the industry's best-selling model in nine months, after Airbus reported defects with fuselage panels last December.
Airbus said it had discovered what it described as a "deviation" in the surface protection or coating applied to skeletal components known as stringers, which run lengthways in a fuselage.
It said the discovery was made while parts were already undergoing rework on the production line.
The latest snag comes as Airbus is trying to increase production of narrowbody jets to 75 a month from about 60 now. Airbus also described that issue as a quality problem with no safety implications, but unravelling the situation caused several months of delivery delays.
Airbus has identified and contained the source of the issue and a remedy is available, it added.
The source said Airbus first spotted the problem over the summer. The first results from closer analysis came back recently.
Customers are continuing to take aircraft deliveries without insisting on extra work being carried out in advance, and Airbus has told customers there is no immediate requirement to repair, the source said.
European regulators may, however, issue a directive formally requiring the defects to be repaired within a certain period.
Delta, which operates A321neo aircraft, said it is "in contact with our OEM partners continually and will always take action to meet or exceed operator recommendations and regulator directives."
Industry publication The Air Current first reported the issue.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police arrest actors, politicians protesting against Netanyahu outside UN
Article:
NEW YORK: Police arrested at least 30 people, including actors and politicians, as they protested outside United Nations headquarters on Thursday against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of his speech at the General Assembly.
Oscar-winning actor Susan Sarandon, Emmy winner Hannah Einbinder, Democratic congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier and New York City Council member Chi Osse were among those arrested.
"What's being done to Gaza, the obliteration of an entire society, in our name, with our tax dollars, this is our responsibility to speak out against, and Netanyahu has no right to use the platform of the United Nations to justify these atrocities," said Manijeh Moradian, a 50-year-old university professor of Iranian and Jewish heritage, who took part in the protest.
At the General Assembly, Netanyahu defended Israel's actions in the region, seeking to counter growing international isolation ahead of elections he could lose, as dozens of delegates streamed out of the General Assembly Hall.
[[nid:1540546]]
The rally was organised by Jewish Voice for Peace, a Jewish activist group that supports Palestinians. Around 200 people gathered outside the United Nations in identical white T-shirts bearing slogans including "Fund people not bombs", "No war" and "Free Palestine".
The group blocked traffic, and police ordered them to leave through loudspeakers. Some people moved to the pavements, but the core group of protesters remained seated on the pavement and continued chanting anti-Netanyahu slogans as police officers, who arrived on bicycles, surrounded them.
One by one, officers pulled protesters from the group, tied their hands behind their backs with zip ties and escorted them to police buses. The activists continued chanting "Netanyahu go to hell" outside the buses.

Title: Trump tells countries to quit ICC. Few follow his lead
Article:
UNITED NATIONS: President Donald Trump urged countries to leave the International Criminal Court immediately, calling it "evil" and a "rogue institution", but only Naoero, a tiny Pacific island nation formerly known as Nauru, has followed suit during the UN General Assembly this week.
Trump's appeal on Tuesday capped an escalating US campaign against the Hague-based court, which Washington says oversteps its authority by claiming jurisdiction over citizens of countries, including the United States and Israel, that have not ratified its founding treaty, known as the Rome Statute.
While a handful of countries have moved to leave the ICC, many governments, particularly in Europe, have rallied to defend it as a cornerstone of international justice. Parties to the statute include 125 countries.
The US has imposed financial sanctions and visa bans on court staff, and officials have prepared sanctions that could undercut the court's ability to operate, sources familiar with the matter said.
'Dismantle the ICC'
In July, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio launched a diplomatic push to "dismantle the ICC — brick by brick, if necessary", claiming the court posed a threat to American service members and those carrying out Trump's deportations of migrants and strikes on alleged drug-trafficking boats.
Trump has said the campaign is aimed at protecting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, against whom the ICC issued arrest warrants in 2024 alongside his then-defence minister and a Hamas military commander over the Gaza war.
Since Rubio announced the campaign, Venezuela and Chad have announced plans to withdraw from the court. Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger announced their exits the previous year, denouncing the court as an instrument of "neocolonial repression".
Naoero President David Adeang said in his speech to the UN General Assembly on Tuesday he would formally withdraw his country from the Rome Statute due to the ICC's "increasing irrelevance".
"Naoero joins a growing number of nations standing up for their sovereignty against the ICC's illegitimate overreach," US Assistant Secretary for East Asian and Pacific Affairs Michael DeSombre said on X after meeting the island nation's deputy foreign minister.
Defending the court
The European Union rallied behind the Netherlands-based court and officials have discussed drawing up a blocking statute in response to potential US sanctions.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told reporters this week the bloc had options to defend the court.
"We have the tools in our toolbox when it gets really serious, how to defend ICC, and here (at the UN) we are rallying countries behind supporting the ICC functioning and the accountability part because it's not only a European issue; it's much broader than that," she said.
Tomoko Akane, the ICC president already under US sanctions, is a Japanese national. Japan's government called the proposed sanctions "very unfortunate" and dispatched an official to The Hague to discuss how it could support her.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi noted Japan's support for the ICC in her address to the General Assembly on Tuesday.
"Since the end of the Second World War, Japan, as a peace-loving nation, has attached great importance to the rule of law in the settlement of any disputes," Takaichi said.
Brian Finucane, a senior adviser at the International Crisis Group, said many countries remain invested in the ICC's mission of accountability, limiting the impact of Washington's campaign against the court. He noted that Russian President Vladimir Putin targeted the ICC after it issued a warrant for his arrest.
"The Trump administration has managed to align itself with Putin in terms of, you know, imposing targeting ICC personnel with sanctions, and of course, Putin would also benefit from the destruction of the court," Finucane said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UN approves resolution on dealing with rising sea levels
Article:
UNITED NATIONS: The United Nations on Thursday passed a unanimous resolution demanding stronger action on rising sea levels, an existential threat for low-lying island nations driven by ocean warming and melting ice sheets and glaciers.
In 2024, global sea levels rose by almost six millimetres, the largest annual increase ever recorded, and they are set to rise by a metre or more by the end of the century without drastic action.
"Sea-level rise is measured in millimetres, but its toll is measured in millions of shattered lives, uprooted communities, and stolen futures," Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said.
"We cannot allow countries and cultures to vanish beneath the waves – or leave the aspirations of billions dead in the water."
The declaration is aimed at bringing new momentum to efforts to tackle the problem – reducing greenhouse gas emissions and providing funding to vulnerable countries to strengthen their resilience plans.
Concretely, it resolves legal issues around what happens to nations when they start to vanish under the waves.
It affirms that maritime zones remain in place even if coastlines recede, and that "once a State is established, the disappearance of one of its constituent elements would not necessarily entail the loss of its statehood."
"For States that are literally defined by the ocean around us, the impact of sea-level rise will be life-altering," said Palau President Surangel Whipps Jr., speaking on behalf of the Alliance of Small Island States.
Small island states have been sounding the alarm since the 1989 Male Declaration on Global Warming and Sea Level Rise and helped develop international law on the issue, he continued, welcoming the declaration as "a genuine achievement."
Even small increments of sea-level rise pose grave risks, explained Tom Mortlock, a senior catastrophe research analyst at Aon.
One centimetre of sea-level rise translates to a metre of coastline retreat.
Projections show that flooding that might occur once every 50 years with sea levels as they are today could happen every three or four years if sea levels rise by half a metre.
Nature-based solutions such as mangroves "can reduce coastal risk, but it can also get to the core problem we have for climate change which is carbon sequestration and carbon mitigation," said Mortlock.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US airlines oppose China's bid to add more flights
Article:
WASHINGTON: The head of industry group Airlines for America said on Thursday that US carriers oppose adding more direct flights from China to the United States, even as Chinese President Xi Jinping raised the idea.
Chris Sununu, who heads the group representing American Airlines, United Airlines, Delta Air Lines and others, said US carriers continue to be hampered by the fact that Chinese counterparts are allowed to overfly Russia on eight flights. He said he had been advocating to Trump administration officials not to give in.
"It's not just a minor thing. It's a huge cost to the airlines to have to go around Russia," Sununu said in an interview.
At an event in Washington on Thursday, Xi raised the idea of increasing flights. Currently, the United States and China each can operate around 50 round-trip flights per week.
"Our two sides may also increase direct flights to facilitate two-way travel and trade," Xi said.
The White House did not immediately comment.
More than 150 weekly round-trip passenger flights were allowed by each side before restrictions were imposed in early 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Until August 2023, Chinese and US carriers could each fly only 12 flights a week between the two countries.
Airlines for America last week opposed Air China's request to operate more scheduled flights because US airlines are effectively banned from flying from the US East Coast to China as they cannot access Russian airspace, while Chinese carriers can do so for eight US flights.
"It's imbalanced. It's unfair," Sununu said. "They already have an advantage with the eight flights. To give them even more of an advantage would be huge," he said. "Don't make it worse for us."
The US in March 2022 banned Russian flights from American airspace after Russia's invasion of neighbouring Ukraine, which prompted Russia to ban US carriers from overflying the country.
The United States has not banned other countries from overflying Russia but struck a deal with China in 2023 that additional flights approved would not do so.
In October 2025, the US Transportation Department proposed banning Chinese airlines from flying over Russia on routes to and from the United States, saying the reduced flight time this practice enables puts American carriers at a disadvantage.
But the proposal faced opposition from other US agencies and was shelved ahead of trade talks with China.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two large pythons captured in Baling over 48 hours
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
BALING: The Civil Defence Force captured two large pythons, including one that had swallowed a goat.
Baling Civil Defence officer Mohd Faizol Ab Aziz said the first python, nearly 10m long and weighing 45kg, was found in front of the Ibu dan Anak rural clinic in Kampung Teluk Teduri on Tuesday.
He said the team received a call about the reptile at 11.58pm.
"The reticulated python was quite aggressive, making the capture challenging. The team caught the python and brought it to the Civil Defence office for temporary safekeeping."
On Wednesday, Faizol said his team captured a 6m, 35kg python that had just swallowed a goat in Kampung Rambong, Pulai.
He said the team received a call at 3.16pm and was deployed to the location at 3.33pm.
"The operation ended at 4pm without incident."
Faizol said both pythons would be handed over to the Wildlife and National Parks Department.
"Changes in weather, temperature and the environment can cause reptiles to venture out of their natural habitats in search of food or shelter.
"If a reptile is spotted, do not attempt to capture it. Contact the Civil Defence for assistance," he said.

Title: Healthcare bodies need more funding, says association
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: The Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM) has urged the government to increase funding for three critical healthcare bodies, warning that sustained underinvestment could weaken oversight and standards.
Association president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh said the Malaysian Medical Council (MMC), Malaysia Healthcare Travel Council (MHTC) and Malaysian Society for Quality in Health (MSQH) formed the backbone of the healthcare ecosystem but faced funding pressures.
The MMC regulates medical practitioners and upholds professional standards, the MHTC drives medical tourism, while the MSQH oversees hospital accreditation, quality improvement and patient safety across public and private facilities.
The association said funding for both councils had not been sufficiently increased, while MSQH continued to operate without direct government funding.
"Without sufficient support, the ability to maintain rigorous standards, enforce governance and improve care delivery will be significantly constrained," it said.
APHM said the growing medical tourism sector — a contributor to national revenue — strengthened the case for reinvesting in regulation, accreditation and quality assurance to ensure sustainable growth.
It said it was ready to work with the Health Ministry and stakeholders to ensure the three institutions received adequate support, adding that strengthening them would reinforce Malaysia's standing as a trusted healthcare system.
