Title: Malaysia Airlines expands China network, digital partnerships
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines Bhd is expanding its presence in China as passenger traffic on its China network rises 27 per cent in the first half of this year, backed by stronger travel demand between Malaysia and the country.
The national carrier carried more than 600,000 passengers on its China services in the first six months of the year, with an average load factor of 84 per cent.
It expects to carry more than 52,000 passengers on flights to and from China during the Golden Week holiday period from Sept 26 to Oct 11, up 21 per cent from the same period last year.
Malaysia Aviation Group Bhd president and group chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A. Bakar said the country remained a priority growth market for Malaysia Airlines.
"The expansion of our network to nine gateways reflects our confidence in its long-term potential."
He also said the airline would continue to invest in its network, fleet and operating capabilities under its Long-Term Business Plan 3.0, while positioning Kuala Lumpur as a gateway to Asia and beyond.
In 2026, Malaysia Airlines restored daily services to Chengdu and introduced new daily flights to Shenzhen and Changsha.
The additions bring its China network to nine gateways, including Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Xiamen, Hong Kong and Taipei.
Its sister airline Firefly Sdn Bhd also plans to launch daily Kuala Lumpur-Kunming services, subject to regulatory approval.
The route will use Boeing 737-800 aircraft, providing a direct connection between Yunnan and Malaysia while giving passengers onward access to destinations through Kuala Lumpur.
The airline is also expanding its digital presence in China through partnerships with technology and travel platforms.
Malaysia Airlines hosted its China Trade Gala in Shanghai on Tuesday, bringing together travel trade and corporate partners as it outlined plans to expand its network and digital presence in the market.
During the event, the airline formalised three memoranda of understanding with Huawei Technologies Co Ltd, TravelSky Technology Ltd and Weixin Pay.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: North Korea vows to keep nukes 'forever'
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
SEOUL: North Korea will keep its nuclear weapons "forever", its foreign minister vowed yesterday, dismissing the South Korean president's renewed calls for a denuclearised Korean Peninsula.
Pyongyang has legally enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state, with its leadership repeatedly declaring the country's atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible.
The foreign minister's remarks came a day after South Korean President Lee Jae-myung told the United Nations (UN) General Assembly he wanted to halt further growth in Pyongyang's weapons capabilities and eventually achieve a Korean Peninsula "free from nuclear weapons".
"I reaffirm and reconfirm in the strongest tone of voice the steadfast will of our state to keep nuclear weapons through all ages," North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui said in a statement carried by the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).
North Korea's status as a nuclear weapons state was "everlasting" regardless of what hostile forces said, she added.
At the UN, Lee — who has repeatedly sought to revive dialogue with the North — also said South Korea would "lay the groundwork" for the resumption of long-stalled dialogue between Pyongyang and Washington.
The South Korean president said last week that United States President Donald Trump "clearly wants dialogue" with Pyongyang.
Trump, who met the North Korean leader three times during his first term, said last month that he planned to meet Kim Jong-un later this year.
Separately yesterday, Pyongyang said it had tested "updated 240mm controlled multiple-launch rockets" on Tuesday.
KCNA said the weapons were capable of striking targets up to 115km away.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Xi and Trump call for peace in lavish White House state visit
Article:
WASHINGTON: Xi Jinping called Thursday for the United States and China to manage their superpower rivalry and keep AI under human control as President Donald Trump gave his Chinese counterpart a lavish welcome at the White House
Trump shook hands with Xi at the start of a day full of pomp and pageantry, but their talks will focus on tense issues – particularly how to handle the rising challenges posed by artificial intelligence.
The 80-year-old US president hailed what he called his "truly great friendship" with the Chinese leader, with whom he has met three times since returning to power last year.
"Working together, President Xi and I have made tremendous strides on the issues facing our two countries," Trump said.
"During this visit, we will also discuss pressing issues concerning security, technology, and super intelligence – SI."
But while billionaire Trump has repeatedly dismissed fears that AI could pose a threat to humanity, Xi took a more measured tone on the issue.
"We have both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control," he said at the White House.
Xi added that the two countries had a "historic responsibility of advancing human development and progress" and should "strengthen communication."
The Chinese leader also announced that a pair of pandas – a traditional symbol of Beijing's diplomacy – would be heading to a US  zoo in a few days.
'STRONG, VIBTRANT AND FIT'
Few breakthroughs are expected during Xi's state visit. Instead the trip is likely to be more about pomp and pageantry as the world's two biggest economies seek to manage their rivalry.
Trump kicked off things by personally greeting Xi at the airport on Wednesday – the first time in more than six decades that a US president welcomed a foreign head of state in person at Joint Base Andrews near Washington.
A formal welcome and a handshake on the White House South Lawn launched Thursday's events, which include a military flyover, talks in the Oval Office, and a state dinner.
Trump had earlier said that the 73-year-old Xi looked "strong, vibrant, and fit," following recent rumors about the Chinese leader's health.
But the warm welcome masks deep tensions over thorny topics including the trade war between the world's top two economies, and Beijing's diplomatic and economic support for Iran.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Wednesday announced a two-month extension of a trade truce that was due to expire in November.
Both sides are keen to avoid plunging back into the trade war sparked by the US president's sweeping global tariffs last year.
IRAN TENSIONS
Trump confirmed on Wednesday that he would discuss his stalled Iran war with Xi, despite earlier playing down reports that Beijing was giving Tehran intelligence.
"I'll be talking about that and many other subjects – but it's all coming along well," Trump said.
Taiwan will also be on the cards, with Trump's words likely to be watched for any sign of diminishing US support for the self-governing island that Beijing claims as its territory.
Xi's visit will wrap up on Friday morning when the two presidential couples have tea at the White House and then visit the National Archives, home to the US Declaration of Independence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Leukaemia-stricken boy's dream of riding in police car comes true
Article:
PETALING JAYA: A four-year-old boy battling leukaemia had his dream of riding in a police patrol car come true today, thanks to the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters.
Hafiz Hilmy Mohd Nor, who was diagnosed with leukaemia in March, had told his father, Hilmy Mohd Nor, 45, of his wish before Make-A-Wish Malaysia stepped in to make it a reality.
Hilmy said the family had long known of Hafiz's fascination with the police, particularly his excitement whenever he saw police vehicles.
"He really loves police cars and the police. Whenever he sees them on the road, he gets excited, especially by the police cars, uniforms and sirens.
"He gets particularly excited when he sees traffic policemen.
"This is what gives him the spirit to fight through his illness," he said after the programme at the Petaling Jaya police headquarters today.
Also present was Make-A-Wish Malaysia royal patron Tengku Zatashah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah.
Hilmy said Hafiz's treatment journey began in March when he was initially suspected of having dengue.
It was later revealed after further examinations that he had leukaemia.
Hafiz underwent treatment at Canselor Tuanku Muhriz Hospital (HCTM), and his condition has since improved after completing chemotherapy.
"The doctor said Hafiz's condition has improved, although follow-up treatment is still ongoing.
"Our family has always been by Hafiz's side throughout his treatment," said Hilmy.
He said patience had been crucial for the family as they navigated the challenges of caring for a child undergoing treatment.
Hafiz's wish was fulfilled through a collaboration between Make-A-Wish Malaysia and the police at the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters.
Besides riding in a police vehicle, he watched a salute and marching demonstration before joining officers on a short patrol in a police car.
The experience was topped off with Hafiz receiving his own child-sized, driveable police car.
Make-A-Wish Malaysia chief executive officer Irene Tan said fulfilling such wishes allowed children facing critical illnesses to briefly put aside the challenges of their conditions and enjoy moments of happiness.
She said Hafiz's love for police cars brought together the police, his family, volunteers and supporters to create a special experience for him.
"Our hope is that this experience will help Hafiz and his family build resilience as he continues his medical treatment," said Tan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man falls from third floor of Ipoh hospital building, in critical condition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A man is in critical condition after falling from the third floor of a building at Hospital Raja Permaisuri Bainun (HRPB) in Ipoh yesterday afternoon.
Ipoh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said police received a report about the incident at about 2.30pm, Kosmo! Online reported.
He said preliminary investigations found that a hospital security guard had noticed a man behaving suspiciously in an emergency staircase.
“The security guard then followed the man before discovering that the victim had fallen from the third floor of the building.
“The victim was subsequently taken to the HRPB Emergency Department for treatment,” he said when contacted here today.
Muhammad Najib said the victim was believed to be a local man aged between 60 and 70, and was not carrying any identification documents.
He said the man was wearing a red short-sleeved T-shirt and black slacks when he was found.
“The victim is still receiving treatment and is reported to be in critical condition.
“Police are appealing to members of the public who have information, have family members reported missing or recognise the victim based on these descriptions to come forward to help identify him,” he said.
Those with information can contact the Ipoh district police headquarters at 05-254 2222 or any nearby police station.

Title: Woman worker dies after being trapped in lifter machine in Telok Panglima Garang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A woman worker died after she was believed to have been trapped in a lifter machine at a premises in Telok Panglima Garang in Kuala Langat yesterday.
According to Kosmo! Online, Kuala Langat district police chief Superintendent Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi said police received a report about the incident from a local man at about 11am.
He said the victim, who suffered serious head injuries, was taken to a nearby health clinic at about 11.20am.
“However, the victim was pronounced dead by a medical officer at the clinic. The body was sent to Banting Hospital for further action,” he said in a statement.
Mohd Akmalrizal said preliminary checks found no criminal element in the incident, while further investigations were ongoing.
Members of the public with information are urged to contact the nearest police station or the Kuala Langat district police headquarters operations room at 03-3187 2222 to assist investigations.

Title: Narrow escape for couple after lorry plunges into ravine at Hulu Terengganu landslide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A husband and wife escaped injury after they managed to get out of their lorry before it plunged into a ravine formed by a landslide along Jalan Aring-Kenyir near the Sungai Deka Elephant Conservation Centre in Hulu Terengganu yesterday.
Hulu Terengganu district police chief Superintendent Sharudin Abdul Wahab said the couple, aged 57 and 55, were travelling from their home in Ajil to Kuala Krai, Kelantan, to collect fruit supplies when the incident occurred at about 3.40pm, according to Kosmo! Online.
“They noticed the landslide when they arrived at the location and immediately stopped the vehicle before getting out to inspect the area.
“The lorry then slid into the collapsed section, believed to have been due to brake failure. The front and rear sections of the lorry were badly damaged,” he said when contacted here today.
Sharudin said checks showed the area had long been gazetted as closed to all vehicles following the landslide.
“Police will record the lorry driver’s statement to assist investigations under Section 79(2) of the Road Transport Act 1987,” he said.
The couple were reported to have been travelling to Kuala Krai to collect fruit supplies from their home in Ajil when the incident occurred.

Title: Anwar: Malaysia finalising measures to protect MSMEs from foreign e-commerce
Article:
HANGZHOU, Sept 25 — The MADANI government is finalising follow-up measures to address the concerns of local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) affected by competition from foreign e-commerce platforms, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the issue was raised directly in bilateral discussions with China’s top leadership, as well as in business meetings during his working visit to the country.
“The MADANI government is finalising follow-up measures to deal with this issue comprehensively, and this matter will be one of the priorities in the upcoming Cabinet Meeting,” he said in a social media post after concluding his working visit to China.
Anwar said he welcomed Premier Li Qiang’s commitment to identify the best way to protect local MSMEs and prevent further impact.
He said the position was also reinforced by assurances from relevant giant companies, including Alibaba.
In another development, he said the MADANI Diplomacy Mission in Shanghai and Hangzhou recorded potential investments worth RM28.6 billion, particularly in high-impact sectors such as semiconductors, mainstreaming of artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, electric vehicles, battery materials, advanced optics, biotechnology and advanced manufacturing.
In addition, the country recorded potential exports to China of RM8.2 billion over one to three years.
Anwar said the visit also provided exposure to new technology and AI applications that should be studied, and from which Malaysia can gain strength from China’s rapid progress.
“The success of this visit has further strengthened Malaysia-China friendship and diversified cooperation that will bring more benefits and prosperity to the people of both countries,” he said.
The prime minister departed for Kuala Lumpur yesterday after completing a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou. — Bernama

Title: HR minister: Malaysia, Nepal agree on new mechanism to curb migrant worker exploitation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Malaysia and Nepal have agreed to streamline their labour recruitment mechanism to ensure a more orderly, transparent and integrity-driven process, while curbing practices that could lead to worker exploitation.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the commitment was expressed during a phone call with his Nepali counterpart, Minister of Youth, Labour and Employment, Ramjee Yadav. The call also touched on bilateral ties in labour and employment.
In a Facebook post yesterday, Ramanan said both sides recognised the need for a more orderly and transparent recruitment mechanism, and to address practices that burden workers with high costs or expose them to exploitation and unscrupulous intermediaries.
“Malaysia remains committed to managing foreign workers based on the principles of integrity, transparency, accountability and worker protection, without neglecting the real needs of our industries and labour market.
“Our principle is clear. The system must protect workers, facilitate employers, and at the same time close off any room for exploitation and abuse,” he said.
Ramanan said Malaysia and Nepal, which have maintained diplomatic ties since 1960, agreed to continue communicating through appropriate bilateral channels to strengthen cooperation in labour and employment.
He also extended his condolences and sympathies to the Nepali government and its people following the tragic loss of life and destruction caused by last month’s devastating floods.
He added that the MADANI government will continue to give serious attention to the fate of 55 Malaysians still uncontactable following the disaster.
According to international media reports, the death toll from the Aug 26 disaster at the Nepal-China border has risen to more than 1,450, with over 6,000 people still missing across both countries. — Bernama

Title: Najib’s family still awaiting house arrest SOP, says daughter
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The family of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has yet to receive any official information, including standard operating procedures (SOP), from the authorities on the implementation of his house arrest.
Nooryana Najwa, one of Najib’s daughters, said neither the family nor his lawyers had received details from the Prisons Department, including on any modifications needed to the residence for the house arrest arrangement, according to a report by
Berita Harian
.
“We have not received any SOP from the Prisons Department. Simply put, we have not received any official information. Our lawyers have also not received any official information. So we are still waiting for information from the Prisons Department,” she said.
“We really do not know. As family members, we have not received any word or information from prison officers,” she said.
Media had previously reported that Najib was expected to serve the remainder of his sentence at his residence in Langgak Duta here, under Prisons Department supervision, with restrictions including limited family visits.
His lawyer Datuk Hasnal Rezua Merican had said the location was chosen because no family members lived there, allowing the property to be used as a prison facility, subject to criteria set by the Prisons director-general.
Nooryana said the Langgak Duta residence had been vacant since her father was imprisoned on August 23, 2022.
“My mother (Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor) lives with me. So the house has been empty since (Najib) was imprisoned,” she said.
Najib is currently serving his sentence at Kajang Prison following a conditional pardon granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim on September 18, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence for the SRC International case under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to the conditions imposed, including payment of a RM50 million fine.
However, as of today, the eighth day since the decision, there has been no new development from Kajang Prison.
On the fundraising campaign launched by Umno, Nooryana said she had been informed that total contributions had so far reached more than RM2 million.
“I understand that Umno members are not concentrated in the cities, so it is quite difficult for us to reach the fundraising target within a short period.
“So, Umno’s effort at the moment is to bring the fund to programmes in rural areas each time to raise more contributions,” she said.
Nooryana said the family welcomed the decision on the conditional house arrest after waiting for some time for developments concerning Najib’s situation.
“At the time of the decision, my mother was with me. We were happy because at least there was a decision. There was a way out for my father.
“Although the opportunity is rather complicated for the family, we know what needs to be done,” she said.
However, she said the family was still waiting for several matters to be finalised before commenting further on the implementation of the house arrest.
“Because right now we are still waiting. There has been no final decision. So I cannot comment beyond that.
“I know there is a lot of speculation out there and so on. If we are to make a decision, we will make it based on accurate information from the authorities,” she said.
Nooryana also said the family was touched by the support shown by Umno and members of the public who had contributed towards efforts to secure Najib’s release through the house arrest arrangement.
“We were very touched when Umno announced that it would launch a solidarity fund for Datuk Seri Najib. Likewise, we appreciate the efforts of members of the public who are willing to contribute.
“We are relieved because there is finally a way out. It gives the family hope, although we understand that its implementation remains subject to the conditions set,” she said.

Title: Planning a weekend trip? KTMB just added 63,000 seats to the KL-Johor ETS route
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is providing four additional ETS services for the KL Sentral-JB Sentral-KL Sentral route every weekend until Dec 27 to meet growing passenger demand for the southern sector.
KTMB, in a statement yesterday, said the additional services will operate on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays over 50 days, offering 63,200 extra seats, with ticket sales opened since Sept 7.
The four additional trips involve the EX9572 service from JB Sentral at 7 am and EX9578 at 5.30 pm to KL Sentral, as well as EX9573 from KL Sentral at 9.05 am and EX9575 at 11.55 am to JB Sentral.
“Ticket sales for the four additional ETS services have reached 46 per cent of the offered capacity as of today. KTMB encourages passengers to book early, especially for weekend travel,” the statement read.
With the addition, KTMB said 12 ETS services are available for the KL Sentral-JB Sentral-KL Sentral route, including eight existing services, bringing the total weekend capacity to 189,600 seats.
KTMB is also providing eight additional EMUPlus services from Sept 25 to 27, with Bandar Tasek Selatan being another option for passengers to start their journey to Ipoh, apart from the Klang Station.
The service offers 2,448 seats for the Bandar Tasek Selatan-Ipoh-Klang and Klang-Ipoh-Bandar Tasek Selatan routes, with tickets on sale since Sept 22.
KTMB said the additional ETS and EMUPlus services were part of efforts to increase capacity and provide more public transport options as weekend travel demand rises, in line with its Road to Rail aspiration.
“KTMB will continue to monitor demand patterns and ticket sales to adjust service capacity according to current needs.
“The public is advised to plan their journeys and purchase tickets early through the KITS Style app, KTMB official website or ticket kiosks at selected stations. Passengers are also advised to arrive early at the station for smoother boarding,” it added. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak expected to gain 15 new parliamentary seats under proposed redelineation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Sarawak is expected to gain 15 new parliamentary seats under a proposed electoral boundary redelineation exercise, which would bring the number of parliamentary constituencies in the state from 31 to 46 and help ensure Sabah and Sarawak collectively account for one-third of representation in the Dewan Rakyat.
Based on proposed electoral boundary documents shared with
Berita Harian
, the increase would raise Sarawak’s parliamentary seats from the current 31 to 46.
The Dewan Rakyat currently has 222 seats, comprising 166 in Peninsular Malaysia and 56 in Sabah and Sarawak, with 31 in Sarawak and 25 in Sabah.
The current 56 seats represent about 25 per cent of the total, compared with 74 seats that would be required if the one-third representation principle under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) were applied.
A further 18 parliamentary seats would be needed for Sabah and Sarawak to reach that figure.
After the formation of Malaysia in 1963, Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore collectively held one-third of the 159 parliamentary seats at the time, with the remainder allocated to Malaya.
Following Singapore’s departure from Malaysia in 1965, the quota was supposed to be shared by Sabah and Sarawak.
A source from a Sarawak political party told BH that the proposed increase had already been submitted by the Election Commission (EC) to local political parties and was now at the public display stage, which is scheduled to end this month.
“The proposed boundary review would see an increase after taking into account the growing number of voters in the state,” the source said when contacted.
According to records on the EC website, the last parliamentary boundary redelineation exercise in Sarawak was carried out in 2005.
That exercise added three constituencies — Igan, Sibuti and Limbang — increasing the total number of parliamentary seats from 28 to 31.
On December 3, 2015, the Sarawak Legislative Assembly approved the current state electoral boundaries, involving amendments to Clause (2) of Article 14 of the Sarawak Constitution that added 11 seats to the existing 71, bringing the total to 82.
For parliamentary constituencies, the amendment did not increase the existing 31 seats but instead changed the name of Mambong (P198) to Puncak Borneo.
Taking into account the eight-year interval, the way is now open for a new boundary review in Sarawak.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had previously said after chairing the Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council meeting in Kota Kinabalu that the government had agreed in principle to amend the Federal Constitution to allow for additional parliamentary representation from Sabah and Sarawak, while increasing the representation ratio for the two states from the current level.
The decision was agreed by the Cabinet and communicated to the EC to begin consultations.
Meanwhile, the EC’s boundary review documents also list 17 proposed new state constituencies across 14 Sarawak parliamentary constituencies, which would increase the number of state seats from 82 to 99.
Ten constituencies proposed for name changes
Based on the documents, among the parliamentary constituencies proposed to receive new state seats are Mas Gading, Santubong, Petra Jaya, Stampin and Kapit.
For example, one new state seat, Jagoi, is proposed for Mas Gading, in addition to its two existing state constituencies, Opar and Tasik Biru.
Petra Jaya, which currently has three state constituencies — Tupong, Samariang and Satok — is proposed to receive two additional seats, Serapi and Semarak.
Overall, the 17 proposed new state seats take into account the demographic composition of the areas, with seven involving Malay, Melanau and Kedayan-majority areas, four for Iban communities, three for Chinese-majority areas and two for Orang Ulu communities.
Besides the proposed new seats, the boundary review also includes name changes for 10 existing state constituencies.
Among them, Opar is proposed to be renamed Serayan, Tasik Biru to Singai, Tarat to Bung Sadung, Jemoreng to Muara Lassa and Bawang Assan to Rassau.
Other proposed changes include Lambir to Pantai Tusan, Jepak to Jepak Jaya, Senadin to Riam and Ba’Kelalan to Gunung Murud.
However, the proposed 17 new state constituencies have yet to be finalised and must go through several legal processes, including objections and local inquiries.
The EC is currently displaying its proposed recommendations for the seventh review of federal and state electoral constituencies in Sarawak from September 1 to 30 for public inspection.
During this period, the state government, affected local authorities and groups comprising at least 100 registered voters may submit written representations or objections with supporting reasons.
EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the commission had so far received 18 representations online, most concerning proposed changes to polling district centres between state constituencies, as well as several objections over the renaming of state constituencies, particularly in Sarikei, Bintulu and Sibu.
He said the EC takes into account several key principles when determining new boundaries, including the number of voters, geographical considerations and local ties.
On whether the proposed new seats could be used at the next Sarawak state election, Ramlan said he expected they would not be ready in time.
“The term of the Sarawak Legislative Assembly expires in February 2027. So, based on the work process we need to go through, I expect we will not be able to use the new number of seats in the next state election,” he said.

Title: On trip to China, Anwar mourns death of elder brother Idrus at home
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 25 — The late Idrus Ibrahim, the elder brother of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, showed no unusual signs before passing away in his sleep at his home in Cheruk Tokkun, here, yesterday.
His daughter, Aida Rafizah Idrus, 54, said her late father, 83, who previously suffered a heart attack last year, had recovered and only had a poor appetite lately.
She said although her late father’s leg strength was no longer as strong as it used to be, he could still get up, walk, and manage himself.
“We really didn’t expect it, didn’t suspect it at all (that he would pass away). The deceased also did not show any signs of illness at noon today. He only ate a little kiwi fruit and a tudung/tepung bungkus cake, after which father said he wanted to rest.
“So he lay down before sleeping and likely wanted to get up to perform the Asar prayer, judging by how he had already placed the sarong used for praying nearby. I tried to wake him up, but at that time he was already unconscious, which was around 5:30 pm,” she said when met at the home of the late Idrus here last night.
Earlier, Anwar through a Facebook post today shared the sad news of his elder brother’s passing while he was on his way back to the homeland after concluding a three-day working visit to China.
Anwar was reported as saying that he was heartbroken for not being able to be by the side of the deceased during his final moments, while also asking the public to offer prayers and recite Al-Fatihah for the late Idrus.
Aida Rafizah, who lived with her late father and mother Faridah Hanim Mohd Ghouse, 80, at the house, said the passing was a huge shock to their family because he did not suffer from any chronic illnesses and previously only went for routine health checkups at the hospital.
She said the medical team confirmed that “my father passed away of old age,” and the family accepts the departure of their beloved father with resignation, despite still being shocked and saddened.
“My brother who lives in Kuala Lumpur and my two siblings in Johor are on their way back here,” she said, pausing several times to hold back tears and cry.
Aida Rafizah, who is the second of four siblings, said funeral prayers for the deceased will be held in the prayer hall of the Cheruk Tokkun Bawah Mosque before he is buried at the Cheruk Tokkun Bawah Cemetery after Friday prayers tomorrow.
The late Idrus was an elder brother of Anwar and leaves behind a wife, four children, and 10 grandchildren. He was the second of eight siblings.
Meanwhile, a Bernama survey at the home of the late Idrus found members of the public arriving to pay their respects, and they also held a tahlil session at the residence.
Additionally, several tents have been erected in the compound of the house, and the Governor of Penang, Tun Ramli Ngah Talib, is expected to pay his last respects to the late Idrus tomorrow.
Police were also present in the housing area to control traffic following the large number of people coming to pay their respects to the deceased. — Bernama

Title: PDRM tightens security at Wisma Negeri following exco revocation
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 25 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), particularly the Negeri Sembilan police contingent, continues to prioritise public safety and order in light of current developments in the state.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said that the PDRM acknowledges the statement from the Attorney General’s Chambers regarding the proclamation dated April 19 and respects the ongoing constitutional and legal processes without making any determinations beyond its jurisdiction.
“PDRM has implemented access management to the Wisma Negeri Office for the former line-up of Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (MMKN) members immediately following the announcement of the cancellation of their appointments made by the Negeri Sembilan Palace.
“This action is to ensure that the aspects of safety, public order, and smooth operations at the premises are continuously maintained,” he said in a statement here yesterday.
Alzafny also explained that the deployment of police at several locations, including the Tuanku Ja’afar Royal Gallery, the Luak Sungei Ujong Hall, and the State Secretariat yesterday, was to maintain public safety.
He said that any access control at the relevant location is implemented in a controlled manner based on the current security assessment and the premises management requirements, in addition to avoiding any situation that could cause tension or disrupt public order.
He said that the action should not be interpreted as the PDRM favouring or recognising any party in matters that are undergoing constitutional and legal processes.
“As an agency responsible for maintaining peace and enforcing the law, the PDRM will continue to carry out its duties professionally, fairly, and based on the law without favouring any party,” he also said.
He added that the PDRM will not compromise on any actions that violate the law, provoke, disturb public order, or threaten the safety of any individual and institution. — Bernama

Title: Rais Yatim expected to be charged in Ayer Keroh court today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Former Dewan Negara president Tan Sri Rais Yatim is expected to be charged at the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court in Melaka today.
A check of the e-Kehakiman portal showed Rais listed for proceedings before Judge Raja Noor Adilla Raja Mahyaldin at 9am, while Rais has also reportedly confirmed the matter when contacted by the media, Astro Awani reported.
Details of the charge, including the relevant legal provision, have not been disclosed.
Rais was reported to have attended a ceremony proclaiming Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan at a hotel in Alor Gajah, Melaka, on June 5.
He later told the media that the process had been carried out according to state customs.
The validity of the proclamation was subsequently disputed.
The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang later affirmed that Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir remained the legitimate Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan and that there was no vacancy in the position.

Title: Haze doesn’t just hurt your lungs: Experts warn of hidden damage to skin, scalp and eyes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — While public health warnings during haze episodes typically focus on respiratory health, medical experts are sounding the alarm on the hidden, often overlooked impact of pollutants on the body’s largest organ: the skin, as well as the scalp and eyes.
As air quality fluctuates, experts told
Malay Mail
that fine particulate matter, known as PM2.5 — particles measuring 2.5 micrometres in diameter — poses a significant risk that goes far beyond surface-level dirt.
According to UM Specialist Centre consultant dermatologist Dr Nik Aimee Azizah Faheem, these tiny particles are insidious.
“Haze is not just the usual dust and pollutants; it has PM2.5 particles which are tiny, 2.5 micrometres in diameter. These particles can penetrate our tissue, be it the skin, lungs, or eyes.
“They don’t just sit on the surface and cause external dirt,” she said.
The invisible damage
When PM2.5 particles infiltrate the pores, they disrupt the skin’s natural barrier.
This leads to increased sensitivity, dryness, and irritation, often triggering flare-ups of underlying conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, and acne.
However, the damage extends deeper.
Dr Kwan Zhenli, a consultant dermatologist and dermatologic surgeon at Subang Jaya Medical Centre, said haze consists of particulate matter from smoke, dust, moisture and vapour suspended in the air that impairs visibility.
“Particulate matter in haze can penetrate the skin, causing oxidative stress and inflammation.
“Haze also alters the skin microbiome composition, which can impair the skin’s barrier function. Air pollutants synergise with UV radiation to worsen oxidative skin damage, as pollution-related changes to the ozone layer allow greater UV transmission to the earth’s surface,” Dr Kwan explained.
This synergistic effect is a major point of concern for dermatologists, who note that many people falsely assume that “cloudy” or hazy skies mean lower UV exposure.
“Many omit their sun protective measures like wearing sunscreen, protective hat, sunglasses and UV-protective clothing, thinking that there is a lack of these harmful UV rays.
“This can lead to long-term photo-damaging effects like pigmentary disorders, wrinkles, and potentially skin cancers,” Dr Nik warned.
Echoing similar sentiment, Pantai Hospital Cheras dermatologist Dr Low Dyoi-E, said the consequences are chronic.
“Prolonged exposure may accelerate premature skin ageing by promoting free-radical damage to collagen and elastin.
“It can also contribute to dullness, uneven pigmentation and weakening of the skin barrier, increasing dryness and potentially aggravating inflammatory conditions such as eczema,” Dr Low said.
Scalp and hair health
The scalp is equally vulnerable.
The PM2.5 particles can block hair follicles, leading to inflammation and scalp congestion.
“On the scalp, these particles can also penetrate and block our hair follicles.
“This can lead to a disruption in our scalp barrier, a buildup of dirt and dead skin cells, as well as an overgrowth of Malassezia furfur, which is a type of yeast that is a normal commensal of our scalp,” said Dr Nik Aimee, adding that this may result in inflamed, itchy, flaky scalp called seborrhoeic dermatitis.
Dr Kwan added that for hair, “particulate matter can trigger inflammatory responses in the hair follicle, causing chemical and oxidative damage that leads to loss of shine, structural weakening and hair loss, including conditions such as alopecia areata.”
Vulnerability of eyes and children
The eyes are also immediate targets for haze-related irritation.
In the short term, exposure leads to dryness, redness, itchiness, and conjunctivitis.
Persistent exposure, however, can be more serious.
“Long-term effects can be in the form of persistent dry eyes, cataract and glaucoma,” Dr Nik Aimee stated.
Children are particularly at risk, given that they are generally more active and have developing immune and respiratory systems.
Dr Kwan emphasised that children are “more susceptible to the effects of haze as they typically spend longer time outdoors, are more physically active, and have developing respiratory systems that are more vulnerable to the effects of particulate matter.”
When should you worry?
While daily precaution is advised, there are specific thresholds for concern.
Dr Nik Aimee noted that for those with pre-existing skin, hair, or eye conditions, an Air Pollutant Index (API) of 50 and above may trigger a flare-up.
For the general population, an API of 100 and above is sufficient to cause dryness and irritation.
Steps to protect yourself
The experts advised a multi-pronged approach to mitigation, starting with the most effective method: avoidance.
“Number one is avoidance; that means to stay indoors and avoid any outdoor activities,” said Dr Nik Aimee.
She also advises avoiding wearing contact lenses, which can trap particles against the eye, and reducing screen time to prevent eye strain and further dryness.
Dr Kwan suggested a comprehensive routine: “Stay indoors as much as possible, use air purifiers, drink plenty of water, and eat a healthy diet rich in antioxidants.”
For skincare, Dr Low suggested using moisturisers containing ceramides, hyaluronic acid or niacinamide, and using antioxidants like vitamin C, vitamin E and niacinamide to help counter oxidative stress.
Both Dr Nik Aimee and Dr Low stressed the necessity of daily sunscreen, regardless of how hazy the sky appears.
“Wash the face and scalp after outdoor exposure; avoid harsh scrubbing,” advised Dr Low.

Title: Beyond reconciliation: How the National Population and Family Development Board helps non-Muslim couples part ways peacefully
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The National Population and Family Development Board’s (LPPKN) Mediator Body Pilot Project extends its support beyond marriage reconciliation, helping non-Muslim couples separate amicably while continuing to fulfil their responsibilities as parents.
Dr Sarada Devi R. Subramaniam, a psychology officer and registered counsellor with LPPKN’s Family Well-being Division (Counselling and Intervention Unit), said the initiative aimed to help couples make mature decisions and understand that their parental responsibilities remained unchanged despite changes in their marital status.
“We don’t force or persuade our clients. We simply give them the space to make mature decisions. You can separate as husband and wife, but you can’t separate as father and mother,” she said during the second season of the KASIH Lensa Keluarga podcast, titled “Bilik Tribunal: Tempat KASIH Diuji, Tempat KASIH Dicari”, which aired last night.
Sarada Devi said the project’s success was not only measured by the number of couples who reconciled, but also by helping those who chose to divorce part ways amicably while continuing to fulfil their responsibilities as parents.
According to her, separating couples must continue to provide financial support and remain involved in their children’s lives, without putting them in the difficult position of choosing between their mother and father, while understanding how prolonged conflict can affect their development and well-being.
The Mediator Body Pilot Project, a collaboration between the National Registration Department (JPN) and LPPKN, provides non-Muslim couples facing marital conflict with counselling and intervention to help them resolve their differences before filing for divorce.
Sarada Devi said the collaboration with JPN enabled registered LPPKN counsellors to assist in handling marriage tribunal cases involving non-Muslim couples by giving both parties a space to share their marital concerns separately.
Couples are then referred to LPPKN for counselling to address the underlying issues affecting their marriage and consider their next steps before attending a joint session to decide whether to continue their marriage or separate.
Sarada Devi said her experience showed that marital conflict often stemmed from communication problems, infidelity, financial difficulties and interference from family members or friends, whose advice could sometimes be biased.
However, she said complaints raised at the start of a session might not always point to the actual cause of the conflict, as financial problems, for instance, could sometimes be linked to emotional neglect.
Sarada Devi said counsellors would provide a safe, confidential and neutral environment for couples to discuss their concerns without fear of judgment, while helping them better understand each other’s emotional needs and love languages, such as appreciation, affectionate touch and quality time.
She added that individuals who come for the sessions alone, such as those whose foreign spouses are overseas and unable to join them, are also guided in planning their post-divorce lives, particularly in managing their finances, careers and responsibilities as single parents.
Sarada Devi advised couples facing prolonged conflict to seek professional help before making decisions about the future of their marriage, and encouraged them to make use of LPPKN programmes such as SMARTSTART to enhance their knowledge and preparedness for married life. — Bernama

Title: Rohingya caught between Malaysia crackdown and Myanmar’s uncertain welcome
Article:
YANGON, Sept 25 — As a Rohingya exile who abandoned his life in Malaysia to return to Myanmar, Ismail’s bleak prospects may portend what awaits others caught in Kuala Lumpur’s migrant crackdown.
Weeks ago, the 25-year-old was eking out a living at a Malaysia fish market, one of legions of the Muslim minority group who left Myanmar to escape violence some monitors say amounted to genocide.
But a wave of anti-Rohingya sentiment, migrant arrests and a government plan to repatriate Myanmar nationals drove Ismail back, even though the nation he fled still denies him full citizenship.
“People without a country like us, we have nowhere to come back (to),” said Ismail, using a pseudonym for security reasons like other Rohingya in this story.
He subsists jobless on the charity of family in Yangon, carrying ID branding him a second-class citizen and cowering from the security forces who spearheaded the crackdown on his people.
“We are the most discriminated people,” said Ismail, “the people from nowhere”.
Nearly 1,500 Myanmar migrants are due to be sent home from Malaysia next week, the first of 5,000 that Kuala Lumpur says agreed to “voluntary” repatriation from detention centres.
Malaysia’s foreign and home ministries have not responded to a query on what proportion will be Rohingya.
But the group makes up two-thirds of the 190,000 Myanmar refugees and asylum seekers in the country, according to the United Nations.
Perilous precedent
The Rohingya left Myanmar en masse starting in 2017 when a crackdown of mass killing, rape and arson began in western Rakhine state.
Rights groups say it was a military-led campaign of ethnic cleansing, a claim the armed forces deny.
The majority of Rohingya -- 1.2 million—now live over the Bangladesh border in overcrowded camps, while Malaysia is the second-largest host nation.
Despite Malaysia being a Muslim-majority country, the Rohingya there are facing pressure, including from an online campaign that rights advocates say is fuelling xenophobia and intimidation.
For years, efforts to repatriate Rohingya to Myanmar have stalled over the ethics of returning them to a country where conditions have only worsened since a 2021 coup that triggered civil war.
Some fear Malaysia’s return scheme will erode existing protections.
“Whether or not Rohingya are among those returned, this could set a troubling precedent,” said one UN official in the region, speaking anonymously because they were not authorised to talk to media.
“Other countries in the region could follow suit despite ongoing risks in Myanmar.”
With many Rohingya sequestered inside detention centres with reportedly dire living conditions, it is hard to judge how voluntary the repatriations are.
“Given the choice, I don’t think anyone wants to stay there,” said Yap Lay Sheng, a senior human rights specialist with NGO Fortify Rights.
“They would rather risk their life and go back home.”
The Myanmar government has pledged a “safe and dignified” welcome. But it is unclear where the Myanmar navy ships slated to carry them will dock, and what their future holds.
Myanmar-based activist Mohammad fears any fellow Rohingya may be dispatched to impoverished and besieged displacement camps in Rakhine.
Four residents recently died there in a suspected cholera outbreak, while both sides of the civil war are accused of atrocities against the Rohingya.
“I feel extremely helpless,” said 26-year-old Mohammad. “They don’t recognise us as human.”
But he struck a note of resilience: “While they don’t count us as people, I still have my own life and hope—because I was born human.”
Bargaining chips
Yap of Fortify Rights said the Rohingya are being treated as “bargaining chips”.
Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is “politically embattled” and “wants to be seen as powerful on immigration enforcement” ahead of elections due by early 2028, he said.
Myanmar meanwhile is seeking favour from Malaysia as it tries to shake off its post-coup pariah status.
Anwar has invited coup leader turned civilian president Min Aung Hlaing for an official visit in a bid to expedite the repatriations.
It would be the first such welcome since the coup for Min Aung Hlaing, named as a chief architect of the Rohingya crackdown in numerous legal cases.
The Myanmar military claims the campaign was targeting insurgents, but the International Court of Justice is weighing whether it constituted genocide.
Caught between a hostile adoptive home and a motherland that denies their rights, Rohingya migrants in Malaysia, like 30-year-old Asif, face an agonising choice.
“I get a headache just thinking about where to go,” he said. — AFP

Title: N. Sembilan Ruler formally revokes appointments of 10 exco members
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir has revoked the appointments of 10 state executive council members, according to a state government gazette.
The gazette said Tuanku Muhriz withdrew his consent and cancelled their appointments after stating that they had breached their oath of loyalty.
It said the 10 Exco members had taken and signed their oath and pledge of loyalty before Tuanku Muhriz on August 7, before taking their seats in the State Executive Council.
According to the gazette, the oath included pledging loyalty to the Ruler and the Royal Institution, protecting and preserving the sovereignty of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution, and recognising the authority vested in the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang.
It said the 10 had breached the oath through their actions and statements on September 15.
The cancellation of their appointments took effect immediately on September 20, 2026, according to the gazette.
The 10 affected Exco members are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Haji Zaifulbahri Haji Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Haji Mohd Asna Haji Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.
The gazette said the revocation was made under Article XXXVIII(5) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959, which provides that a State Executive Council member other than the Menteri Besar holds office for as long as the Ruler consents.
The gazette was issued as the Government of Negeri Sembilan Gazette, dated September 20, 2026.

Title: High Court to rule Oct 23 on bid to stop RHB closing shipping firm’s accounts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The High Court here today fixed October 23 to rule on a shipping company’s bid to restrain RHB Bank Berhad from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit.
Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P. Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank’s counsel, Gan Khong Aik.
Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts.
He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care.
Gan countered that no fiduciary relationship or duty of care arose between the bank and the shipping company, submitting that the relationship between a bank and its customer is that of debtor and creditor.
In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company’s application for a full injunction.
According to court documents, the company has held a multi-currency account and a current account with RHB since 2005.
On October 6, 2025, it received a termination notice dated October 1, 2025, stating that the bank intended to close both accounts and terminate all related services within 14 days, citing breaches of its internal policies and guidelines.
The company, however, claimed that RHB had failed to specify which policies or guidelines were allegedly breached.
The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025.
The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application.
The appellate court then ordered RHB to produce its Minimum Due Diligence guidelines governing foreign-exchange transactions to the company within 45 days.
Maritime Network further alleged that the bank’s vague allegations placed it in a position of uncertainty, depriving it of any opportunity to defend itself.
This conduct, the company asserted, amounted to an abuse of power that prejudiced its rights.
It also claimed that the bank’s conduct demonstrated an intention to oppress rather than protect its legitimate banking interests. — Bernama

Title: MACC, FBI step up cooperation to tackle corruption, cross-border crime, says chief commissioner
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 24 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) are reinforcing their cooperation through the exchange of experience and expertise, as well as capacity-building in enforcement.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said this was among the matters discussed during a courtesy visit by an FBI delegation led by Law Enforcement Attaché Varinder Singh to the MACC headquarters here today.
“Strategic cooperation with the FBI is an important platform for strengthening enforcement capabilities through the sharing of experience, expertise, and best practices, besides benefiting the capacity-building of MACC officers,” he said in a statement today.
Abd Halim said the nearly hour-long meeting focused on operational issues, including corruption linked to fraudulent activities and coordination between enforcement agencies in addressing cross-border crime challenges.
He said the visit also opened up opportunities for both sides to explore new areas of cooperation that could be strengthened in the future.
“The opportunity to participate in various programmes and training conducted by the FBI is invaluable,” he said.
Also present were MACC senior directors Datuk Y.S. Karunanithy (Special Operations Division), Datuk Saiful Ezral Arifin (Intelligence Division), and director Datuk Saiful Hazmi Mohd Saad (Legal and Prosecution Division), as well as FBI Assistant Law Enforcement Attaché Cody Kirk. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: BN to negotiate with other parties soon, says Ab Rauf
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 24 — Negotiations for cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and other parties for the 16th Melaka State Election are expected to be held soon, says Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Chief Minister, said the negotiations would begin as soon as he receives the green light from the top Umno and BN leadership.
“There will definitely be negotiations (with other parties),” he told reporters after attending an appreciation ceremony for Melaka state government retirees here today.
Ab Rauf said the 21 state seats won by BN in the 15th state election would form the basis of the coalition's negotiations.
“That is the basis of our negotiations. Meaning, that is our right, and we can negotiate on the rest. That is the baseline,” he said.
On Tuesday, Ab Rauf announced the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly, which took effect yesterday (Wednesday).
Meanwhile, Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus, in a statement yesterday, said domestic and international postal voting applications for the 16th Melaka State Election opened yesterday for all categories.
He said all applications must be made online via the MySPR portal at https://myspr.spr.gov.my, and that the closing date will be announced later. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, China agree on proposed ECRL extension to Rantau Panjang, says Anwar
Article:
HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Malaysia and China have agreed on the proposed extension of the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang, Kelantan, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the project would not only stimulate economic activity in the remote areas of Kelantan which had previously been left behind, but would also establish a direct transport link with Thailand.
“Further discussions on the ECRL proposal will be held with all stakeholders before it is brought to the Cabinet for consideration,” Anwar told the Malaysian media at the conclusion of his working visit to China today.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said he also received positive feedback on the proposal during his discussions with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul.
The 665-kilometre ECRL is a land transportation project providing fast cross-regional services connecting the West Coast and East Coast of Peninsular Malaysia.
The ECRL route, starting in Kota Bharu and ending at Port Klang, will link 20 stations, including 10 passenger stations and another 10 stations that will combine both freight and passenger transport.
Also present at the press conference were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Transport Minister Anthony Loke, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, and Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad.
Anwar said today’s bilateral talks with Premier Li Qiang were highly important as they covered strategic issues facing both countries and the Asean region, as well as providing information on the key agenda items for the meeting between United States President Donald J. Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, who is currently on an official visit to Washington, DC.
Asked whether the issue of tariff restrictions and trade pressure from the US was discussed, Anwar said that Malaysia remains neutral and has chosen to maintain direct dialogue with the US, with China being fully aware of the matter.
Meanwhile, he also extended his heartiest congratulations to the 22 Malaysian participants competing at the 48th WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, which will run until the end of this week.
Earlier, Anwar also officiated the Malaysia Pavilion at the Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo at the Hangzhou Grand Convention and Exhibition Centre.
The Malaysia Pavilion, which brings together 15 exhibitors including four government agencies, highlighted Malaysia’s strengths and innovations across digital trade, artificial intelligence, cloud services, smart healthcare and cross-border e-commerce.
The Malaysian companies’ participation, which was coordinated by the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade), showcased the capabilities and strengths of country’s digital and tech-based companies competing in the global arena.
The Prime Minister departed for Malaysia at 4.15pm local time after ending his three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, China. — Bernama

Title: Tengku Zafrul asks N. Sembilan MB to name who allegedly forced him to sign proclamation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has been urged to explain who allegedly forced him to sign the Instrument of Proclamation regarding the position of Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir on August 3.
Senior Political Advisor to the Prime Minister Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz said the question remained unanswered despite Ismail issuing a seven-page statement on the issue.
He said while the statement maintained that the government did not determine who ascends or abdicates the throne, it failed to explain the Menteri Besar’s sudden change in stance.
“Is it true you were forced to sign the proclamation on Aug 3? If so, who forced you?” Tengku Zafrul asked in a Facebook post today.
Earlier, Ismail claimed that he and the former state executive council had never made a decision to dethrone or appoint the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, but merely discussed the state administration’s stance on the proclamation submitted as a decision of the Undang Yang Empat.
Tengku Zafrul said the issue was not a small matter as a Menteri Besar had claimed to have been forced to sign a document related to the Ruler’s position, and had even lodged a police report over the matter.
He noted that Ismail was sworn in as Menteri Besar before Tuanku Muhriz on August 2, just a day before signing the Instrument of Proclamation regarding the abdication.
“However, more than a month after the signing, on September 6, Ismail still expressed his full support and loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz as the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
“On September 9, he said the signature on the proclamation was made unwillingly and under duress. The state government at the time took the stance that the proclamation did not meet the stipulated processes and procedures,” he added.
Tengku Zafrul also questioned what had changed that led to the state executive council meeting chaired by Ismail on September 15 reportedly taking the stance that the proclamation was valid and enforceable.
“What caused the change in stance? Were you also forced, as you claimed when signing the Proclamation? If there was pressure to change your stance, who was involved and who did you meet during that period?” he asked. — Bernama

Title: Former Petronas manager met Petros official before job interview, court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The Sessions Court today heard that former Petronas manager Mohd Khairul Akmal Mohd Jasni met informally with a senior official of Petroleum Sarawak Berhad (Petros) at the Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club (KLGCC), before a formal interview for a position at the company in 2024.
The fifth prosecution witness, a former Petronas employee, said the meeting took place before Mohd Khairul Akmal’s interview with Petros chief financial officer and chief executive officer, Mohd Azha Abdul Jalil and Datuk Janin Girie, respectively, at the company’s office in Kuching, Sarawak.
“He met Mohd Azha at the KLGCC before the formal interview, but I am not sure of the date,” the witness said during examination-in-chief by deputy public prosecutor Noor Syafina Mohd Radzuan in the trial of Mohd Khairul Akmal, who faces a charge of attempting to disclose a report to Petros in June 2024.
The witness said Mohd Khairul Akmal applied for the position of Head of Upstream Finance at Petros in 2024, while he was Manager of Business Planning Performance Review Upstream at Petronas.
When questioned by Noor Syafina whether the two positions were similar in terms of scope of duties, the witness replied, “There are similarities.”
Noor Syafina:
To your knowledge, do you know the salary scale for this position at Petros?
Witness:
I don’t quite remember, but he asked me how much he should request, and I gave him some advice. I suggested how much he should ask from Petros at the time.
However, the witness, whose name is withheld under the law, did not remember the suggestion given at the time.
The witness, who served with Petronas for 12 years, said that under the Petronas Code of Ethics, employees of the company must obtain prior approval before sharing any sensitive information, such as emails relating to the company.
“If you are referring to the sharing of sensitive company information, approval must first be obtained from the parties involved. As employees, we cannot share confidential and sensitive information without approval,” the witness said.
Mohd Khairul Akmal, 41, is accused of attempting to disclose information, namely, a document titled “Q1 2024 Upstream Business Performance Operational & Financial”, to Petros at a condominium in Jalan Pinang here, between 3.19pm and 3.21pm on June 8, 2024.
He had allegedly obtained the document while serving as Manager of Business Performance for a Petronas business unit.
The charge is framed under Section 203A(1) of the Penal Code, read together with Section 511 of the same Code, which provides for a maximum fine of RM1 million or imprisonment of up to one year.
However, Section 511 caps any custodial sentence at half that term upon conviction.
The trial before Judge Mazuliana Abdul Rashid resumes tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: Anwar’s elder brother Idrus Ibrahim dies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today shared the sad news of the death of his elder brother, Idrus Ibrahim.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said he received the heartbreaking news while returning to Malaysia from a three-day working visit to China.
“It is difficult for me to express this sense of loss when someone who shared so many memories throughout my life is now gone. Only Allah SWT knows how heavy my heart is in accepting this reality.
“I regret not being able to be by his side in his final moments, but I accept this with resignation even as my heart is still trying to come to terms with a separation we were never prepared to face,” he said.
The prime minister also prayed for the deceased to be forgiven for his shortcomings, showered with mercy and placed among Allah’s faithful servants who do good deeds.
He also asked the public and friends to offer prayers and recite Al-Fatihah for the deceased.
“Thank you for all the memories and kindness he left behind, all of which will remain etched in our memories and hearts,” he said.
