Title: Man rams traffic policeman, injures him while fleeing Ipoh roadblock
Article:
IPOH, Sept 24 — A traffic policeman suffered a fractured arm and leg after being rammed by a car that attempted to flee during a roadblock inspection on Jalan Silibin, here, this morning.
Ipoh District Police Chief ACP Muhammad Najib Hamzah said that during the 9.45am incident, police managed to arrest the 29-year-old man after his car skidded at the Taman Wing Onn traffic light junction.
He added that initial investigations revealed that during the inspection, a traffic officer from the Ipoh District Police Headquarters (IPD) ordered the car to stop, but the driver failed to comply with the instruction and sped away from the location.
“Three traffic personnel then pursued the car. Upon arriving at the traffic light area near the Perak State Secretariat (SUK) Building, the driver entered the left lane before making a sudden U-turn and ramming into a traffic personnel.
“The driver then fled towards Gunung Lang, and upon reaching the area near McDonald’s Gunung Lang, the driver drove against the flow of traffic before his car skidded at the Taman Wing Onn traffic light junction,” he said in a statement today.
Muhammad Najib said that as a result of the incident, the traffic personnel suffered a broken left arm and right leg and was taken to Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital (HRPB) for further treatment.
He added that further investigations on the male driver revealed that the suspect did not possess a driver’s licence, the vehicle’s road tax had expired, and an initial urine screening test on the suspect came back positive for methamphetamine.
“Further investigations are still underway, and the case is being investigated under Section 44(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987,” he said.
Earlier, an 18-second video went viral on social media showing a white vehicle moving at high speed, hitting a road divider, driving against the flow of traffic, and crashing into several vehicles on Jalan Kuala Kangsar, Ipoh. — Bernama

Title: Rapid KL to offer free shuttle buses for Bahrain GP at Sepang
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 24 — Rapid KL, in collaboration with Sepang International Circuit (SIC), will provide free shuttle bus services in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the SIC from October 2-4.
Ninety-five buses will be deployed for the free shuttle service on a loop basis, thereby ensuring convenient and comfortable movement of visitors from key locations to the event venue.
Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the special shuttle bus service to SIC would operate from three locations, namely the bus hub at Level 1 of the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 2, the Mitsui KLIA bus hub and De-Village, Persiaran Millenia 2, Bandar Baru Enstek.
“The service will operate from 7 am to midnight on all three days, with a frequency of between 10 and 15 minutes. To complement the service, Rapid KL will also provide shuttle buses within the circuit to facilitate visitors’ movement to key locations.
“The provision of these services reflects Rapid KL’s commitment to supporting the hosting of international-standard events and encouraging the use of public transport,” he said in a statement today.
To ensure smooth and safe operations, all buses will undergo safety inspections and be monitored continuously throughout the service period.
Rapid KL personnel will be also stationed at strategic locations around the event venue to assist visitors and manage passenger movements.
He also advised visitors to plan their journeys in advance, follow instructions from personnel and queue when using the shuttle bus service.
Further information regarding the routes and operating schedules of the shuttle bus services can be obtained through Rapid KL’s official website and social media channels.
Malaysia will host the F1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP at SIC, marking the first time in F1 history that a race has been relocated to another country following its cancellation.
F1 said in a earlier statement that the event, which is subject to final agreement and official approval, including from the FIA World Motor Sport Council, would be known as Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar: China visit yields RM28b in potential investments across high‑tech sectors
Article:
HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Malaysia has secured more than RM28 billion in potential investments following trade talks with major Chinese industry players, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The commitments were secured during a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, which included a roundtable discussion with 21 companies and targeted meetings with five Chinese industrial giants.
The high-impact investments span several strategic sectors, including semiconductor manufacturing, artificial intelligence, robotics, electric vehicles, biotechnology, and advanced medical devices.
“The vast majority of these companies expressed their commitment to increasing investments due to their confidence in our stability and the policies we are currently implementing.
“Overall, these business meetings recorded potential investments valued at over RM28 billion,” said Anwar.
The Prime Minister made the announcement following the launch of the Malaysia Pavilion at the 5th Global Digital Trade Expo at the Hangzhou Grand Convention and Exhibition Centre here today. — Bernama

Title: Emrail loses RM59m LRT3 bond suit, ordered to pay Kuwait Finance House RM39m
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — In a double courtroom defeat for rail contractor Emrail Sdn Bhd, the High Court has dismissed its RM59.1 million lawsuit against Kuwait Finance House (M) Bhd (KFH) and ordered the company alongside three personal guarantors to pay the bank RM39.09 million.
Justice Quay Chew Soon dismissed Emrail's claim over a disputed performance bond for the Light Rail Transit 3 (LRT3) development in its entirety and allowed KFH’s counterclaim in full, holding the contractor and its guarantors jointly and severally liable for the outstanding debt,
FMT
reported.
The three personal guarantors ordered to satisfy the judgment debt are prominent corporate figures Zaki Azmi, Hari Narayanan Govindasamy, and his son, Amrish.
The litigation turned on whether KFH was contractually bound to issue a performance bond conforming strictly to the template prescribed by MRCB George Kent Sdn Bhd (MRCBGK), the project delivery partner (PDP) for the LRT3 project.
“The central question underlying the plaintiffs’ claim is not what the employer wanted, but what the defendant (KFH) agreed to do,” Quay ruled in his judgment issued today.
The judge held that the underlying Islamic financing facility expressly stipulated that the Kafalah bank guarantee had to be in a form, and addressed to parties, acceptable to KFH. This contractual term gave KFH unfettered discretion to decide whether the wording and structure of the requested bond were acceptable.
The court further established that the specific performance bond template required by Emrail was never incorporated into the financing agreement with KFH.
Quay ruled that Emrail could not rely on its independent construction contract with MRCBGK to enforce obligations against KFH, which was not a party to that agreement.
“The plaintiffs have conflated Emrail’s contract with its employer/PDP and its financing contract with the defendant,” he said.
The court also rejected Emrail’s argument that KFH had acted negligently by failing to issue a compliant bond, ruling that a claimant cannot use the tort of negligence to extract a more favourable commercial bargain than what was negotiated under contract.
On Emrail’s claim that the lack of a compliant bond caused RM59.1 million in interim project payments to be withheld, the judge found that the contractor failed to establish causation. The court noted that Emrail offered no proof that MRCBGK would have certified or released the sums, observing that other LRT3 contractors faced industry-wide payment arrears, with Emrail itself eventually receiving around RM402.5 million under a subsequent contract for the rail project.
Ruling on KFH’s counterclaim, Quay held that the financing facility expired on Oct 31, 2021, leaving an outstanding debt of RM39,089,705.42 as of May 16, 2025.
The court ordered Emrail and the guarantors to settle the sum within one month, alongside post-judgment interest at 5 per cent per annum from the date of the decision until full settlement, and awarded KFH RM100,000 in legal costs.
Lawyers S. Shaarvin Raaj, A. Anusha, K. Ravvenneah, J. Jeyakrishna, and Iman Nur Alya represented Emrail and the guarantors.
Counsel Syed Faisal Al-Edros Syed Abdullah, Mohd Wafiy Azman, Choo Shi Jin, Nasbal Harun, Ahmad Iqbal Rohaizan, and Wardah Yunus acted for KFH.

Title: Air quality dips in Sarawak with nine areas unhealthy, Melaka also affected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — A total of nine areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 4pm today, with the Serian District Police Headquarters (IPD) recording the highest reading at 200.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, other areas that recorded unhealthy readings were Kuching (188), Samarahan (179), Sri Aman (172), Bintulu (162), Sarikei (157), Sibu (156), Samalaju (155) and Kapit (133).
Meanwhile, 48 areas recorded moderate readings, including Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur (75); Keningau, Sabah (60); Seberang Perai, Penang (53); and Kota Bharu, Kelantan (52). Another 11 areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 is moderate, 101 to 200 is unhealthy, 201 to 300 is very unhealthy, while 301 and above is hazardous. — Bernama

Title: MCMC backs police crackdown as Op Pedo nets 53 suspects, eight of them teens
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 24 — The collaboration between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) continues to be strengthened to combat the misuse of network services for the purpose of online child sexual exploitation.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC, as the technical agency, would continue to play an important role in assisting PDRM, especially the D11 Division (Sexual, Women and Child Investigation) of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), in tracking down those who misuse network services and subsequently bringing them to justice.
“The MCMC’s role is to ensure that anyone who misuses network services can be traced, arrested and brought to justice, especially those who prey on children and women,” he told Bernama and RTM after attending the Communications Ministry’s ‘Jasamu Dikenang’ (Appreciation) ceremony here today.
Fahmi said the collaboration also involved technical and forensic aspects to assist PDRM investigations into online child sexual exploitation activities.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said on Sept 22 that eight teenagers, including a 13-year-old, were among 53 individuals arrested for suspected involvement in activities related to child sexual abuse material (CSAM) under Op Pedo Integrated 3.0 conducted recently.
The suspects were detained in simultaneous operations conducted from Sept 14 to 16 following intelligence gathered by the CID’s D11 unit with the MCMC, with police also detecting activities involving the production, distribution and sale of CSAM-related videos and animations through closed online groups, with the material being offered for between RM50 and RM60.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said the MCMC was also placing emphasis on the safety aspects of social media platforms through the legal framework related to online safety.
“Through the Online Safety Act, we are also emphasising to social media platforms the need to ensure that the environment or platform itself remains safe, especially for women and children, notably those below the age of 16 are not allowed to open social media accounts,” he said.
Regarding the appreciation ceremony, which honoured 157 retirees and soon-to-retire employees from the Communications Ministry, Fahmi said the experience and insights of retired civil servants should continu to be utilsed to help improve government services, especially in the field of communications.
“I pray that they will continue to find ways to share their views and contribute to ensuring the government’s efforts, especially in the communications, remain successful in the eyes of the people.
“If there is anything they wish to share with us for improvement, I am very open to receiving their feedback,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Sabah sees 10 million searches on Xiaohongshu as China tourism interest surges
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 24 — Sabah has recorded over 10 million searches on REDnote (Xiaohongshu), China’s leading social and lifestyle platform, signalling a massive surge in interest from Chinese travellers, said Datuk Jafry Ariffin
The Sabah minister of tourism, culture and environment disclosed the figures following his visit to the REDnote office in Shanghai yesterday, noting that the high search volume underscores Sabah’s strong visibility in the Chinese market.
“This is a very encouraging indication for Sabah. The interest is already there, and our focus now is to turn that interest into actual visits,” he said.
According to the minister, the platform’s users are most captivated by Sabah’s iconic sunsets, rugged mountains, pristine seas and fresh seafood.
Jafry believes this digital traction presents a prime opportunity to convert online exposure into physical arrivals as the state builds momentum for Visit Sabah 2027.
“We want more Chinese travellers to experience Sabah for themselves, from our spectacular sunsets and Mount Kinabalu to our islands, fresh seafood, wildlife and diverse cultures,” he added.
The minister said that digital ecosystems like REDnote are now pivotal in shaping travel decisions, especially for younger, independent travellers who shun traditional tour packages in favour of peer recommendations.
“China remains an important tourism market for Sabah. As we strengthen air connectivity, our destination marketing must also reach travellers through the platforms they use to discover and plan their holidays,” he said.
The trip to Shanghai is part of a broader strategic engagement in China to tighten industry partnerships and improve market access, ensuring Sabah remains a top-of-mind destination for the region.

Title: Masidi confident Putrajaya will secure Sabah borders amid Balabac Strait concerns
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 24 — Sabah Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun is confident the federal government will safeguard the state's borders in the Balabac Strait, despite concerns surrounding a US-backed Philippine military facility in the region.
Speaking to reporters after the Sabah Carbon Forum today, Masidi said that border security falls under the jurisdiction of Putrajaya.
“It’s under their authority. So, definitely, I’m very sure that our government has done all that is necessary and reasonable to make sure that our borders are well-guarded,” he said.
When asked if Sabah would see additional security reinforcements, Masidi replied, “All I can say is that I don’t think they will allow Sabah to go undefended.”
The minister urged the public to remain objective, warning against statements that could spark unnecessary speculation. He stressed the need for a measured approach to the geopolitical development.
“I don’t think we should emotionalise the issue because there are a lot of issues that are related to that. I think the most important thing is that Sabah is not in any way exposing itself to security breaches just because somebody is building a huge facility.
“We should look at it with a reasonable and cool head. We don’t want to issue a statement that will somewhat lead to a lot of speculation,” he added.
The concerns stem from the upgrade of a Philippine military facility on Balabac island in southern Palawan, situated near the Balabac Strait that separates the Philippines from Sabah. Under the Enhanced Defence Cooperation Agreement, the US is supporting the development, which includes a 3km airstrip.
This expansion has heightened security sensitivities in Malaysia, particularly given the Philippines’ longstanding claim over Sabah, a claim that Kuala Lumpur firmly rejects.
Regarding a meeting held on September 11, Masidi declined to disclose specific details, noting only that the discussions covered various matters in the best interest of Sabah and the nation.
